statement: Without total energy in the model (Y ~ N + C), a nutrient's coefficient estimates the effect of absolute intake, which total energy confounds through body size, physical activity, metabolic efficiency and reporting scale, so under inference this model is sound only as a stated crude or sensitivity model beside an energy-adjusted one.

statement: A model that holds a total-energy column in any role (energy, covariate or exposure) is the standard energy-adjusted model, whose nutrient coefficient is at fixed total energy; so 'no energy adjustment' requires every total-energy column (by role or by name) to leave the model, and the estimand must be read off the fitted matrix rather than the method's name.

decision: which columns enter the model under 'none'; the estimand sentence and row meanings
user_sees: energy_kcal reads as total energy and is in the model as a covariate, so each nutrient's coefficient is at fixed total energy (the standard model), not an absolute intake.
claimed_basis: audit ME-02 ('build the estimand sentence from the fitted matrix, not from the method's name')
notes: Other locations: describe_model energy.py:1644-1661; total_energy_columns energy.py:1483-1493; warning text in stages/modeling.py:708-714. Near-definitional; the test checks the coefficient equals statsmodels' standard model and that 'excluded' gives the unadjusted one. Relies on the name recognizer (reads_as_total_energy) to find energy kept under another role.

statement: The standard model, both residual forms and both density forms give a nutrient coefficient that is biased even without confounding (composite variable bias: total energy enters as a composite of sources with unequal effects), and every energy model other than all-components only partially accounts for confounding by common dietary causes (Tomova et al. 2022).

Density alone's caveat list omits the composite-bias line, but its sound label says 'severely biased'.

statement: With total energy kept in the outcome model, the linear, unstratified Willett residual N_adj = N − b(E − Ē) and E span the same columns as N and E, so N_adj's coefficient (point estimate and interval) equals the standard model's exactly, in the nutrient's own units (the Willett–Stampfer variant; McCullough & Byrd 2023).

The test compares with statsmodels' standard model (1e-10, CI 1e-8) on one fixture. The estimand text is the same for every family: a penalized family (ridge or elastic net) is not invariant to this reparametrization, so the identity does not hold there. MODELING_SEQUENCE §2: a spline or categories on a residual breaks the identity (handled in exposure_form). For the stratified variant see S1-041.

statement: In the energy-dropped residual model Y ~ N_adj + C, the nutrient's coefficient equals the standard model's only when no other covariate correlates with total energy; otherwise it is a different number, which can differ in sign, and its interval is wider.
regime: residual method with total energy left out of the outcome model; covariates present

user_sees: kcal left the outcome model: each nutrient's coefficient is the standard model's (with kcal kept) only when no covariate correlates with kcal.
claimed_basis: audit ME-03 ('show the gap'); McCullough & Byrd 2023
notes: coefficient_gap at energy.py:2108-2138 fits both models on the same rows (OLS or logit) for the card. The test is partial: it shows a sign flip on one fixture against statsmodels (+0.0199 vs −0.0067); test_energy.py::test_residual_and_standard_models_give_the_same_nutrient_coefficient shows equality with no covariates. 'Its interval is wider' is untested and not guaranteed: var(N_adj | C) ≥ var(N | E, C), so when E explains little of Y the energy-dropped SE can be smaller. 'Only when' holds exactly only for sample orthogonality of C and E.

MODELING_SEQUENCE §2: a log on an energy component conflicts with reading a substitution as a coefficient difference.

statement: In the energy partition model Y ~ kcal_from_N + kcal_from_other + C, the nutrient's coefficient is the total effect of adding calories from N with every other source fixed (an addition, not a substitution), and it is unbiased only when there is no confounding by the other sources or when all the other sources have equal effects (Tomova et al. 2022).

statement: In the all-components model (each energy source its own kcal term, plus kcal from other), each source's coefficient is its total effect, and its average relative causal effect (the substitution for the average of the other sources) is θ_j = β_j − Σ_k w_k β_k, with w_k each other source's mean share of the remaining energy (survey-weighted under a surveyed population), reported per unit of the nutrient.

user_sees: protein_g in place of the other energy sources, weighted by their share of the remaining energy (carb_g 59%, fat_g 41%): the average relative effect, per g
claimed_basis: Tomova et al. 2022 ('subtracting a weighted average of the estimated effects of all other individual component sources of energy'); audit ME-14
notes: Also METHOD_TABLE energy.py:251-267. The test is a known-truth simulation (truth 0.0305; estimate 0.0307 with a CI covering it) plus a by-definition contrast in statsmodels. MODELING_SEQUENCE §2: the all-components contrast is undefined on logged components. MS3: 'an exact pooled linear contrast for all-components'.

statement: θ_j equals the coefficient of x_j after replacing each other energy term x_k by x_k + w_k·x_j, an invertible change of columns that leaves the fit, residuals and leverages unchanged, so the family's own coefficient table (HC3, CR2 or Firth) gives θ_j a valid interval, with the weights w_k treated as fixed constants.
regime: all_components under inference; any family with a coefficient table
decision: interval of the average relative effect
user_sees: protein_g_relative row with estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p
claimed_basis: algebra in the docstring (reparametrization)
notes: Code at energy.py:2074-2095. Partial: the test checks the interval against HC3 written out by definition with w fixed; CR2 and Firth are not checked, and neither the app nor the test accounts for the sampling variability of w (estimated from sample means). Firth's invariance relies on the Jeffreys penalty being equivariant under linear reparametrization.

statement: A total-energy column whose median daily value lies in the kilojoule range (about 7,000–11,000) is in kJ rather than kcal (typical intake 1,600–2,600 kcal), so an energy partition, which subtracts kcal from it, is refused until it is converted.
regime: partition methods without a usable Atwater reconstruction
user_sees: the partition subtracts kcal from energy, and its median daily value is in the kilojoule range (7,000–11,000), not kcal; convert it to kcal first
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §01 magnitude prior ('energy 1,600–2,600 kcal (7,000–11,000 kJ)'); audit IN-07
notes: A kJ-named energy column is refused outright at energy.py:556-557. The rule lives in recognizers.energy_unit_by_magnitude.

statement: Because general Atwater factors run only a few percent off a food table's specific ones, a 'kcal from everything else' remainder below zero by more than 5% of total energy on more than 10% of rows means the chosen nutrients overlap or are not in grams, and the partition is refused.
regime: partition methods
decision: whether the partition can run on these columns and rows
user_sees: fat_g and carb_g carry more energy than energy_kcal itself on 412 of 3,000 rows, so they overlap or are not in grams.
claimed_basis: none stated (thresholds stated in comments)
notes: Check at energy.py:671-679; counts kept at 896-904.

statement: A partition (or all-components model) that includes a macronutrient total together with one of its own parts counts the part's energy twice, so it is refused, with the totals-only partition offered when that passes the other checks.
regime: partition methods with nested columns among the nutrients
decision: whether the partition can run; the offered alternative
user_sees: fat_sat is a part of fat_total, so a partition would count fat's energy twice.
claimed_basis: none stated (energy accounting)

statement: The all-components model needs every energy source the table holds as its own term: protein, carbohydrate and fat always, and alcohol whenever the table carries an energy-bearing alcohol column; so it is refused when any of these is not among the chosen nutrients.
regime: all_components method
decision: whether the all-components option can run
user_sees: The all-components model gives every energy source its own term, and fat is not among the chosen nutrients.
claimed_basis: Tomova et al. 2022 ('simultaneously adjusting for all dietary components')
notes: Fiber is not required (ENERGY_SOURCES[:3]). When the named sources make up total energy exactly, kcal_from_other is dropped (energy.py:774-782).

statement: A nutrient already expressed per unit of energy (percent of energy, per 1,000 kcal, a density) must not be residual- or density-adjusted again, since that puts energy into the model twice.
regime: residual and density methods with a density-unit nutrient
user_sees: fat_pct_kcal is already expressed per unit of energy; adjusting again puts energy into the model twice.
claimed_basis: none stated
notes: test_energy.py::test_an_energy_share_is_not_adjusted_for_energy_again checks the refusal only. Standard and partition are not refused for density nutrients by this check.

statement: Every quantity the energy step learns (the N ~ E residual slope and centering, the partition's unit checks) must be learned only from the rows the step is fitted on: training-fold rows inside cross-validation under prediction, every analyzed row under inference; fitting the residual regression on training plus test rows before cross-validation leaks information.
regime: energy step inside a cross-validated or refit pipeline
decision: where the residual regression is fitted
user_sees: Each of fat_g is regressed on energy_kcal within the fitting rows; the model sees the adjusted nutrients with energy_kcal beside them.
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §04 anti-pattern ('fitting the N ~ E residual regression on train+test before cross-validation'); BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 3
notes: Also energy.py:720-722 (missing stays missing). test_energy.py::test_inside_cross_validation_fit_sees_only_training_fold_rows checks the mechanism only, not that leakage would bias anything.

statement: In the within-strata residual (e.g. within sex), adding back one constant for every level (the pooled prediction of N at the mean energy of all fitting rows) makes N_adj uncorrelated with energy and with the strata column on the fitting rows, so a model without the strata column does not read between-level differences as the nutrient's effect, whereas adding each level's own mean manufactures that spurious effect.
regime: residual method with strata; strata column possibly not a predictor
decision: how the stratified residual is computed
user_sees: …the residual of fat_g ~ energy_kcal within each level s of sex, plus one constant for every level, the predicted fat_g at the mean energy_kcal of all 3,000 fitting rows…
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §04 ('with the predicted nutrient at the cohort mean energy added back'); audit MA-02
notes: Also energy.py:43-49, 1281-1298. The test is a known-null simulation (1,000 replicates, p > 0.05 in ≥95%, |r| < 0.05, unbiased) with a positive control. Uncorrelatedness is exact only for levels with their own slope; a level on the pooled slope is not uncorrelated within itself (test_wp3::test_2 shows r ≠ 0 for it).

statement: A stratum with fewer than 30 fitting rows (or constant energy) cannot pin down its own residual slope, so it uses the pooled slope, centered on its own means.
regime: residual method with strata; small levels
decision: per-level slope in the stratified residual
user_sees: Level X of sex has 29 analyzed rows, fewer than the 30 a residual regression of its own needs, so fat_g is adjusted there with the pooled slope, centered on the level's own means.
claimed_basis: 'A stated floor, not a sourced one: the audit's proposal (AUDIT_REPORT §5, WP3)'
notes: Code energy.py:1121-1149; notes() energy.py:1367-1390. test_wp3::test_4 checks the mechanism only.

statement: The within-strata residual with total energy kept in the outcome model has the standard model's estimand: its nutrient coefficient is the standard model's exactly, because the residual and total energy span the same model as the nutrient and total energy.
regime: residual method with strata (e.g. within sex) and total energy kept
decision: estimand sentence and row meanings shown for the stratified residual
user_sees: The standard model's substitution, with the nutrient in its own units: the residual and total energy span the same model as the nutrient and total energy, so the coefficient is the standard model's …
claimed_basis: none specific to strata (inherits McCullough & Byrd 2023 from the pooled residual)
notes: Implicit: StratifiedEnergyAdjuster.estimand() returns METHOD_TABLE['residual'] (energy.py:1392-1396); describe_model gives form 'residual' whatever the strata (energy.py:1597-1602, 1703-1704) and swap rows 'total energy fixed' (1757, 1815); stages/modeling.py:702 adds no strata wording. With level-specific slopes b_s and level constants, N_adj = N − Σ_s 1[s]·b_s·E + level constants, which lies in the span of (N, E, C) only if every b_s is equal and the strata indicators are covariates. test_wp3::test_1_the_null_holds_with_sex_in_the_model_too uses y ~ within-sex residual + energy + age + sex as its reference, not the standard model.

statement: Total carbohydrate 'by difference' (USDA and NHANES totals) already contains fiber, but food tables disagree on whether total carbohydrate includes fiber; so fiber is never read as a nested part of carbohydrate, and fiber beside total carbohydrate as energy-bearing predictors draws a warning that fiber's energy may count twice in kcal accounting and that a swap through fiber also moves carbohydrate.
regime: fiber and total carbohydrate both energy-bearing predictors
user_sees: fiber_g sits beside carb_g: if carbohydrate is by difference (total carbohydrate, as in USDA and NHANES tables), it already holds fiber, so fiber's energy counts twice in kcal accounting and a swap …
claimed_basis: audit B19
notes: Also nesting.py:16-17. test_wp6::test_4b checks that the warning appears.

statement: A column is a nested part of a macronutrient total when its name names a subtype of the total's macronutrient (saturated, mono-, polyunsaturated or trans fat; sugars, starch, sucrose, fructose, lactose; animal, plant, vegetable or dairy protein) and its values are at most the total's on at least 99% of at least 10 rows where both are recorded.
regime: dietary tables carrying totals beside components
decision: which columns are treated as parts of which totals (partition refusal, swap carrying, remainder labels)
user_sees: On every row, fat_sat, fat_mon and fat_poly are parts of fat_total and moved with it in proportion, so their shares of fat_total held.
claimed_basis: none stated
notes: Code nesting.py:26-41, 90-124. Sucrose, fructose and lactose are parts of sugars, which are themselves parts of carbohydrate; the detection flattens the hierarchy to one parent.

statement: When a substitution moves a macronutrient total that the table holds beside its parts, the coherent move carries the parts in proportion (each part's share of the total holds), and when it moves a part, its total moves by the same amount while the other parts hold; moving a total with its parts fixed is not a coherent substitution.
regime: substitution through a nested total or part
decision: how the shifted rows are built
user_sees: On every row, fat_sat, fat_mon and fat_poly are parts of fat_total and moved with it in proportion, so their shares of fat_total held.
claimed_basis: none stated
notes: Shift at substitution.py:136-153, 247-264; nesting.py:3-6; percent_energy.py:117-129. Proportional carrying is a modeling choice of which swap to estimate. test_substitution.py::test_moving_a_total_moves_its_parts_in_proportion... checks the mechanism only.

statement: A substitution between a macronutrient total and its own part moves no energy (the kcal moved go nowhere), so the pair is refused.
regime: donor and recipient where one is nested in the other
decision: whether the substitution pair is accepted
user_sees: fat_sat is part of fat_total, so moving energy between them moves nothing; choose two separate nutrients.
claimed_basis: none stated
notes: Also nesting.py:5-6.

statement: Averaging the curve at each k only over rows whose shifted donor and recipient stay within their observed [min, max], stay non-negative, and (when total energy is named) keep each moved column's share of energy within its observed range keeps the curve from extrapolating off the observed diet composition, which a uniform shift otherwise does like a PDP (300 kcal put 22% of rows off support).
regime: any substitution curve
decision: which rows each point of the curve averages over
user_sees: Rows whose shifted fat_g or carb_g would leave the observed range or go negative, or whose share of energy from either (of energy_kcal) would leave the range of that share observed, are left out at …
claimed_basis: PRODUCT_VISION §06c; audit MA-13; Scholbeck et al., arXiv:2201.08837, App. A.2
notes: Code substitution.py:266-304. The checks are marginal (each column's range and each share's range), not joint support. test_wp5::test_4 counts the masks by hand (computation only).

statement: The substitution curve stops at the first k where fewer than 50% of rows remain on support.
regime: any substitution curve
user_sees: …the curve stops at the first k where fewer than 50% of rows remain; that 50% floor (min_support) is a practitioner convention, not a sourced threshold.
claimed_basis: 'A practitioner convention, not a sourced threshold'
notes: Default min_support=0.5 at substitution.py:325, 907; note 826-829. The implied reason is that beyond it the average describes a minority of rows.

statement: Because each k's average uses its own on-support rows, the per-k curve mixes the effect of k with the change in which rows remain; averaging over the rows on support at every k the curve reached (the fixed-population curve) removes that mixing.
regime: any substitution curve whose support shrinks with k
decision: the second (fixed-population) curve and its note
user_sees: Each k averages over its own on-support rows, so the rows behind the curve change with k; the fixed-population curve averages over the same 3,912 rows, those on support at every k up to 300 kcal.
claimed_basis: audit B17
notes: Code substitution.py:435-439, 502-520, 834-837. test_wp5::test_4_a_fixed_population_curve_averages_the_same_rows_at_every_k checks the computation only.

statement: A band from refitting the whole pipeline on bootstrap resamples of the fitting rows carries the uncertainty of fitting the model and has approximately nominal coverage for the substitution contrast, whereas a band from resampling rows through one fitted model has zero width for a linear model and reads as certainty.
regime: substitution curve with a band asked for (no surveyed population)
decision: how the curve's band is made
user_sees: Refits that succeeded: Linear model 200 of 200.
claimed_basis: audit MA-12; AUDIT_REPORT §5 WP5
notes: refit_band substitution.py:547-616. Also turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp5_substitution_band.py::test_1_at_n_10000_the_band_half_width_is_within_15_percent_of_the_analytic_one. Both use a linear model only. Refits are pinned to the full fit's tuning (pinned_to_full_fit, stages/modeling.py), so tuning uncertainty is not in the band.

statement: A percentile bootstrap interval needs about 1,000 or more refits, while a normal interval from the refits' standard error settles with far fewer (about 200), so the band uses the percentile interval only from 1,000 successful refits and the normal interval below that, with 200 refits by default.
regime: substitution band
decision: which interval the band uses and how many refits are offered
user_sees: the curve ± 1.96 standard errors of 200 refits
claimed_basis: Carpenter & Bithell 2000, Stat Med 19:1141 (B 1,000–2,000 for 90–95% intervals); Efron & Tibshirani 1993 §6.4 (B = 200 for a standard error)
notes: Verdict at substitution.py:637-648; BAND_BOOT = 200 at stages/modeling.py:41-44. test_wp5::test_2 supports the adequacy of the 200-refit normal band on one linear fixture, not the threshold itself.

statement: A bootstrap band whose failed refits are dropped is conditioned on the resamples a model could be fit on; with at least 90% of refits succeeding this barely moves it, but with more failures it describes another population of resamples, so no band is drawn below 90% success.
regime: substitution band with failing refits (e.g. a resample missing a class)
user_sees: 171 of 200 refits succeeded; a band needs at least 90% of them
claimed_basis: 'A practitioner convention, not a sourced threshold'
notes: Code substitution.py:637-648. test_wp5::test_3_a_band_needs_a_stated_minimum_share_of_successful_refits checks the refusal only.

statement: When each refit draws m of n units, the spread of the m-unit refits times sqrt(m/n) estimates the spread at n for an estimate with root-n error, including the curve's averaging over a subset of rows, so the band is rescaled by sqrt(m/n) and centered on the full-sample curve.
regime: fitting rows above BAND_ROWS (10,000), or a resample size below the unit count
decision: the band's width on large tables
user_sees: (band caption states the resample size and the rescaling)
claimed_basis: Bickel, Götze & van Zwet 1997, Statistica Sinica 7:1-31
notes: Code substitution.py:702-712, 764-772; BAND_ROWS at stages/modeling.py:38-41. The test's '2000-rows-rescaled' case compares with statsmodels' analytic SE. The rescaling assumes root-n behavior of the averaged contrast, which a non-smooth learner may not have.

statement: With repeated rows per unit, resampling whole units (all of a participant's rows together) gives the band the right uncertainty, and a row whose unit is not recorded is treated as a unit of its own.
regime: rows that repeat per unit or cluster
decision: how bootstrap resamples are drawn for the band
user_sees: (band caption names the units resampled)
claimed_basis: none stated here; MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 ('a bootstrap by unit')
notes: Also substitution.py:556-560, 693-722; class_substitution.py:255-259. test_substitution.py::test_a_grouped_band_resamples_whole_units checks the mechanism only.

statement: With 1,000 or more refits, the band from curve − (median − lower percentile) to curve + (upper percentile − median) of the refits, rescaled by sqrt(m/n), is a valid percentile interval placed around the curve.
regime: substitution band with ≥1,000 successful refits
user_sees: (band endpoints)
claimed_basis: none stated
notes: Code substitution.py:768-772. A recentered hybrid of the percentile and basic intervals, not a textbook one. Used only when n_boot ≥ 1,000 (the default is 200). test_substitution.py::test_the_refit_band_is_the_percentile_or_normal_interval_of_the_refits_coefficient_gaps checks the computation only.

statement: For an outcome with three or more unordered classes, the sound substitution estimand under both inference and prediction is one curve per class: the average change in that class's predicted probability (the average discrete change; Long & Freese 2014) when k kcal move isocalorically, over a stated population.
regime: multiclass outcome; two energy-bearing exposures with settled kcal per unit
decision: the Recommended option of the multiclass substitution contract
user_sees: One curve per class: the average change in each class's predicted probability — Sound: a marginal, isocaloric contrast on the probability scale over the stated population; the curves sum to zero at …
claimed_basis: Long & Freese 2014, ch. 8; Stata margins; R marginaleffects
notes: Module docstring substitution.py:50-63. turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_multisub_class_curves.py::test_1_each_class_curve_agrees_with_numpy_multinomial_refits checks the computation against an independent NumPy multinomial fit, not the choice of estimand.

statement: Multinomial relative-risk ratios against a reference class per kcal swapped are not a substitution estimand to offer: they are conditional on every covariate, describe how the odds of a class against the reference move rather than any class's probability, and are a single number only when every energy source enters as a linear term.
regime: multiclass outcome
decision: the reference_ratios option (not offered under either purpose)
user_sees: Conditional on every covariate and against one reference class: it says how the odds of a class against the reference move, not how any class's probability does, and it is one number only when …
claimed_basis: none stated beyond 'as categorical-outcome analyses report them'

statement: Because each row's class probabilities sum to one before and after the move and every class is averaged over the same rows and weights, the K class curves sum to zero at every k; a set that does not is a defect in the predictor, raised and never drawn.
regime: multiclass substitution curves (point, fixed-population and pooled)
user_sees: The class curves sum to zero at every k, because each row's class probabilities sum to one.
claimed_basis: Long & Freese 2014 (average discrete changes sum to zero across outcomes)
notes: Also substitution.py:53-58, 948-949, 1132-1133, 1414-1415. The bands need not sum to anything.

statement: Under inference with multiple imputation, each completed copy's class curves come from that copy's own fit (a family with no coefficient table is refit on each copy) and are pooled at each k by Rubin's rules (T = Ū + (1 + 1/m)B) on Barnard & Rubin's degrees of freedom, with the design df as the complete-data df under a survey and a large-sample df otherwise, which gives valid intervals for the pooled curve.
regime: inference; multiple imputation; multiclass outcome
decision: how class curves and their bands are pooled
user_sees: Each class's curve is pooled over the 20 imputations: each copy's class curves, pooled at each k by Rubin's rules …
claimed_basis: Rubin 1987; Barnard & Rubin 1999; MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 and MS3 ('per copy, pooled per k')
notes: Also substitution.py:64-67; class_substitution.py:13-15, 223-231, 330-498. Partial: the test reproduces Rubin's rules and the bootstrap written out in NumPy (the code computes F); no coverage check.

statement: Each imputed copy's bootstrap standard error (n_boot refits split over the m copies, at least 10 per copy, normal interval) is a valid within-copy variance for Rubin's rules (MI then bootstrap; Schomaker & Heumann 2018).
regime: inference; multiple imputation; a band asked for; no surveyed population
decision: within-copy variance of the pooled class curves
user_sees: …with each copy's bootstrap variance as its within-copy variance (200 refits split over the copies; Schomaker & Heumann 2018).
claimed_basis: Schomaker & Heumann 2018, Stat Med 37:2252
notes: Also class_substitution.py:330-344, 501-517. With 10 refits per copy each copy's SE has about 24% relative error, averaged in Ū. The multisub MI test reproduces the computation only.

statement: Under inference, a substitution curve computed on one fill of the blanks leaves out the imputations' uncertainty, so whenever the missing-values answer blocks the coefficient table or no imputed copies were drawn for the fit, every curve is blocked and recorded, with complete cases (its assumption stated) and a family whose table draws the copies as exits.
regime: inference with blanks among the curve's inputs
decision: whether any substitution curve is drawn
user_sees: No curve is drawn: under multiple imputation every estimate shown under inference is pooled over the imputed copies, and a curve on one fill of the blanks would leave out the imputations' uncertaint …
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 ('A single-fill curve under inference is a defect (MS3)')
notes: Notes at substitution.py:70-74, 1304-1312; relation 1536-1551. turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_multisub_class_curves.py::test_3_with_no_imputed_copies_drawn_no_curve_is_drawn_on_one_fill checks the block only. Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 'A single-fill curve under inference is a defect (MS3)'.

statement: Under a surveyed-population estimand, each class's curve is the survey-weighted mean change from a pseudo-maximum-likelihood multinomial logit, and Graubard & Korn's (1999) linearization of the predictive margin, with the design's variance of a total (PSUs within strata, domain rows scored, other rows zero) on t with the design df, gives its design-based interval.
regime: inference; survey answer 'the surveyed population'; multiclass outcome; linear family
decision: how class curves and bands are computed over the surveyed population
user_sees: …each class's curve came from the survey-weighted multinomial fit, averaged with the weights, with its band by Taylor linearization over the survey design (Graubard & Korn 1999)
claimed_basis: Graubard & Korn 1999, Biometrics 55:652; MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 6; MS4
notes: Also class_substitution.py:298-327. The test compares with R (VGAM::vglm, survey::svyrecvar) to 1e-6 and with a JKn jackknife within 5%; it is skipped without Rscript.

statement: Under inference every curve must come from a fit on every analyzed row, so a family fit only on the training rows (one with no coefficient table, such as boosted trees) is refit on every analyzed row before its curves are drawn.
regime: inference; a family with no coefficient table
decision: which fit a family's curves read
user_sees: Boosted trees: refitting on every analyzed row
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 3 (the seal is purpose-scoped)
notes: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_multisub_class_curves.py::test_1_a_family_with_no_likelihood_draws_its_own_class_curves checks the mechanism only.

statement: The k−1 columns x and x_j = ((x−t_j)/kd)₊³ + [(t_{k−1}−t_j)((x−t_k)/kd)₊³ − (t_k−t_j)((x−t_{k−1})/kd)₊³]/(t_k−t_{k−1}), kd = (t_k−t₁)^{2/3}, j = 1…k−2, are Harrell's restricted cubic spline (Hmisc::rcspline.eval norm = 2, as rms::rcs builds it): they span the natural cubic spline with knots t₁…t_k and are linear beyond the outer knots.
regime: any numeric column declared as a spline or mass-at-zero spline, inference or prediction
decision: functional form of a continuous exposure or confounder (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5)
user_sees: Coefficient rows named `x`, `x'`, `x''` ("as rms prints them"); lineage "restricted cubic spline, 4 knots".
claimed_basis: Harrell 2015, Regression Modeling Strategies 2nd ed. §2.4.5; Hmisc::rcspline.eval / rms::rcs (module docstring)
notes: Independent references: R Hmisc/rms basis to 1e-10, and turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp12a_splines_quintiles.py::test_1_the_spline_spans_patsys_natural_cubic_spline_and_is_linear_in_the_tails (patsy cr span and zero second differences in the tails).

statement: Given only k, knots belong at Hmisc::rcspline.eval's default places, which are Harrell's conventional percentiles: R type-7 quantiles at 0.10/0.50/0.90 (k=3), 0.05/0.35/0.65/0.95 (k=4) or 0.05/0.275/0.50/0.725/0.95 (k=5) of the fitting rows' values. With fewer than 100 values the outer knots move to the 5th smallest and 5th largest values. A lowest (or highest) value held by at least 5% of rows (fractied), when no interior value is that common, becomes a knot of its own, and the other knots are placed on the remaining values.
regime: a spline on any numeric column; knots learned on the rows each fit sees
user_sees: "knots of fiber_g at 12.1, 25, 41.3 and 70.2 (the 5th, 35th, 65th and 95th percentiles)"; notes such as "with 60 values (fewer than 100), the outer knots are the 5th smallest and 5th largest"
claimed_basis: Harrell RMS (rcspline.eval defaults); NUTRITION_PACK §07G ("3 knots at 10/50/90, or 4 at 5/35/65/95"); MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5 ("knots at Harrell's percentiles of observed values")
notes: Also turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_form_2_rcs_rule_and_r.py::test_2_knots_and_basis_agree_with_r_rcspline_eval_and_rms_to_1e_10. These tests show the placement equals rcspline.eval's (a software reference). Whether these locations are methodologically good is Harrell's recommendation and is not tested. KNOT_PERCENTILES is at :84.

statement: Under inference, a spline declared without k should get k = 3 knots when the effective sample size is below 30, k = 5 when it is at least 100, and k = 4 otherwise (Harrell's rule). The same thresholds apply to the effective sample size of every outcome type. k is re-derived whenever the analyzed rows change (an exclusion, complete cases, the consumers-only domain). k is not chosen by AIC, because AIC reads the outcome.
regime: inference; any outcome type; spline declared without k (k = 4 when no effective n can be read)
user_sees: "k = 5 by Harrell's rule (3 knots below an effective sample size of 30, 5 from 100, else 4; here 1,200, the number of analyzed rows)"
claimed_basis: Harrell RMS §2.4.6 (quoted: k = 4 "a good compromise"; "n ≥ 100 with a continuous uncensored response variable, k = 5"; "< 30, say ... k = 3"); the review / MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5 ("k=4 by default; 3 for small n; 5 for large n"; AIC uses the outcome)
notes: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_form_2_rcs_rule_and_r.py::test_2_k_is_harrells_rule_on_the_effective_sample_size only pins the code's thresholds. Harrell states the n ≥ 100 / k = 5 guidance for a continuous uncensored response. Applying 30/100 to min(events, non-events), to event counts and to the ordinal formula is the app's extrapolation. Other locations: rule_stale :877, complete_spec :2338, proposal :1331, rule_words :295. Inconsistency to check: methods/levers.py:51-52 (prediction's Harrell rule, S5 entry) gives 5 knots only ABOVE 100 (n > 100), while this rule gives 5 at n >= 100.

statement: The sample size that limits a model is n for a numeric (or multiclass) outcome, the smaller of the events and non-events for a yes/no outcome, the number of events for a time-to-event outcome, and n − Σnᵢ³/n² over the levels of an ordinal outcome (Harrell RMS §4.4, Table 4.1).
regime: inference; the outcome on the analyzed rows
decision: effective sample size read by the knot rule
user_sees: "...; here 137, the smaller of the events and the non-events)"
claimed_basis: Harrell RMS §4.4, Table 4.1 (docstring)
notes: This is a by-definition test: the formulas are written out from Harrell's text, so it checks that the code computes them. Using n for an unordered multiclass outcome is the app's choice; a referee should check Table 4.1's entry for polytomous outcomes.

statement: Under inference, a restricted cubic spline (k by the rule, knots at Harrell's percentiles) is the soundest declared form for a continuous exposure or adjusted continuous confounder. It is a smooth curve with few parameters, linear in the tails, and carries a test of nonlinearity. It therefore ranks above a straight line, quintiles, declared categories and a data-derived cut point, and the one-tap answer proposes it for every column asked.
regime: inference; continuous exposure or adjusted continuous confounder
decision: functional form of a continuous exposure or confounder (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5)
user_sees: Restricted cubic spline (recommended): "Sound: a smooth curve with few parameters, linear in the tails, with a test of nonlinearity; knots at Harrell's percentiles of the fitting rows."
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §07G ("now near-default"); Desquilbet & Mariotti 2010; MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 2 ("The spline ranks first") and §1 row 5
notes: Ordering tests (turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp12a_splines_quintiles.py::test_1_under_inference_the_spline_ranks_first_and_quintiles_are_tagged_customary; test_form_4 card test) check order and rung only. The contract option is at :2525 and the one-tap proposal at forms_card :1449.

statement: Under prediction, a declared spline is recommended because it nests the straight line. The straight line is available. Quintiles, declared categories and a data-derived cut point (searched inside each training fold) rank lower because cutting discards the variation within each group. Without a declaration, each predictor enters as each model family takes it.

decision: functional form of a continuous exposure or confounder (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5)
user_sees: "Weak for prediction: five steps discard the variation within each fifth."; optimal: "Searched inside each training fold; still discards the variation on each side."
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §4 (rank lower under prediction); contract option "Sound: nests the line" (:2525)
notes: The form gate under prediction is at :1271: "Under prediction each predictor enters as each family takes it; the spline benchmark is on the shelf..."

statement: Under inference, quintiles of a continuous exposure estimate a coarser contrast rather than a false number: they discard the variation within each fifth and assume a step at each cut. They therefore rank below the spline (and the straight line) but are not blocked.
regime: inference; continuous exposure
decision: functional form of a continuous exposure or confounder (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5)
user_sees: Quintiles (rank lower): "Weaker for inference: cutting a continuous intake into fifths discards the variation within each fifth and assumes a step at each cut..."
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 2 ("a coarser contrast, not a false number"); NUTRITION_PACK §07G; Turner 2010 (contract :2537, "the field's primary-analysis convention")
notes: For a confounder the order is spline, linear, categories, quintiles, optimal (:1090). Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 2 (quintiles rank lower, not blocked; spline first; optimal cut points and <=3-group confounders block-and-record, see S2-020, S2-021).

statement: Under inference, beside a declared exposure's spline, the app refits the same model with the spline replaced by four quintile indicators and reports each quintile against the lowest as the customary companion table. The cut points are type-7 quintiles of the fitting rows, the lowest quintile is the reference, and the boundaries are stated (STROBE 16b). This is the table readers expect alongside the spline.
regime: inference; declared exposure with a spline form
decision: quintile table produced by default beside the spline
user_sees: "Beside the spline: quintile 2 of `fiber` against the lowest, +0.12, p = ...; quintile 1: `fiber` ≤ 12.1 (the reference); ..."
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 2 ("the quintile table is produced beside it by default"); NUTRITION_PACK §07G ("quintiles remain expected alongside"); STROBE 16b
notes: The test is a NumPy HC3 refit of the stated design: it checks that the companion is computed as described. That the table is expected is a ruling or convention. design_forms :932 sets the companion flag. The card text is at :1455: "Quintiles are produced beside the spline...". Under MI the cut points are placed on observed values and fixed across copies.

statement: The p for linear trend across quintiles is computed correctly by scoring each row with its quintile's median (medians of the fitting rows) and entering that score as one continuous term in place of the four indicators. Its coefficient is tested on the model's own covariance. The quintile number (1–5) is not used as the score.
regime: inference; quintile form, or the companion quintiles beside a spline
user_sees: "The p for linear trend (customary) across quintiles of `fiber`: each row scored by its quintile's median (..., from the fitting rows), entered as one continuous term ..."
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §08 ("using the median of each quintile as a continuous score, not the quintile number"); MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5
notes: The test checks statsmodels HC3 on a hand-built median score, so it shows the code computes the pack's procedure. Also turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_form_3_5_tests_and_quintiles.py::test_5_the_p_for_linear_trend_is_labeled_customary_and_agrees_with_a_numpy_refit. The companion trend is at :1943.

statement: For a spline, the Wald test that all k−1 spline coefficients are zero is the test of the exposure's association with the outcome. The Wald test that the k−2 nonlinear coefficients are zero is the test of nonlinearity. These are rms::anova's exposure row and its 'Nonlinear' row.
regime: inference; spline form; covariance HC3, cluster-robust, model-based or design-based
decision: which test is reported as the test of association
user_sees: "The test of association: Wald test that all 3 terms of `fiber` are zero (HC3 covariance): F(3, 791) = 4.10, p = ..."
claimed_basis: rms::anova; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5 ("the overall test is the test of association")
notes: Also turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_form_2_rcs_rule_and_r.py::test_2_a_numeric_outcomes_tests_agree_with_rms_anova_on_hc3 and turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp12a_splines_quintiles.py::test_1_spline_tests_match_statsmodels_hc3_f_tests. These are software references for the statistic.

statement: For quintiles or declared categories, the test of association is the multi-df Wald test that every indicator is zero, on the table's own covariance (pooled by D1 under multiple imputation).
regime: inference; quintile or categories form
decision: global test of a categorized exposure
user_sees: "Wald test that all 4 quintile indicators of `fiber` are zero (HC3 covariance): F(4, 790) = ...; quintile 1: `fiber` ≤ 12.1 (the reference); ..."
claimed_basis: MS2 (code comment); MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (form tests pooled by D1)
notes: The reference covers only the MI pooling (mitml D1). No complete-data reference test of the global test was found; test_ms4 checks only its design df structure.

statement: Under inference, after a non-significant nonlinearity test the spline must not be replaced by a straight line. Dropping the curve after its test inflates the type I error of the test of association (by about half; Grambsch & O'Brien 1991). The overall spline test stays the test of association, and a later switch to linear is recorded as made after the estimates were seen.
regime: inference; spline declared
decision: whether a straight line is refit after the nonlinearity test
user_sees: "A non-significant result does not refit a straight line: dropping the curve after its test inflates the test of association's type I error (Grambsch & O'Brien 1991, Stat Med 10:697)."
claimed_basis: Grambsch & O'Brien 1991 Stat Med 10:697; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5
notes: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_form_3_5_tests_and_quintiles.py::test_3_a_non_significant_nonlinearity_test_keeps_every_spline_term checks the behavior (no refit), not the inflation. "About half" appears only in the docstring (:44). Other locations: form_sentence :2027 and contract relation no-silent-linear-refit (:2574).

statement: For a least-squares table with HC3 covariance, the joint Wald statistic W = bᵀV⁻¹b over q coefficients, referred as W/q to F(q, n−p), holds approximately nominal size, unlike a classical-covariance F test. For example, the nonlinearity test at n = 300 with heteroscedastic errors stays near 0.05.
regime: inference; least-squares family with HC3 table
decision: reference distribution of joint form tests (spline, quintile global, interaction heterogeneity)
claimed_basis: none stated in the code beyond "the table's own covariance"; the test docstring cites its own simulation
notes: A known-truth simulation: 600 datasets, size ≤ 0.08 at nominal 0.05, power ≥ 0.90. The computation is also checked against statsmodels f_test (HC3, use_t) and rms::anova with HC3. _reference is at :1504.

statement: With a cluster-robust covariance over G clusters (CR2, CR1, or the Cox model's CR0 Lin–Wei sandwich), the joint Wald test of q coefficients is appropriately referred to F(q, G−1) with F = W/q, as Stata does.
regime: inference; repeated rows within units (cluster-robust table)
decision: reference distribution of joint form tests and interaction heterogeneity under clustering
user_sees: "CR2 cluster-robust covariance by `site` (G = 24), on G − 1 denominator degrees of freedom as Stata does"
claimed_basis: "as Stata does" (no citation)
notes: Used by interaction heterogeneity too (turbotab/core/methods/interaction.py:1066 via wald_test). With few clusters, CR2's small-sample literature (Pustejovsky & Tipton 2018, HTZ test) differs from F(q, G−1); a referee should judge adequacy. No test found.

statement: With a model-based (information) covariance, such as a logistic or Cox model, the joint Wald statistic bᵀV⁻¹b is referred to χ²(q), q = rank(V).
regime: inference; model-based table (logistic, Cox, ordinal)
decision: reference distribution of joint form tests
user_sees: "Wald test that all 3 terms of `x` are zero (the model's information): χ²(3) = 12.40, p = 0.006"

notes: Also turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp12a_splines_quintiles.py::test_1_spline_tests_on_a_binary_outcome_match_statsmodels_logit_wald. These are software references.

statement: For a logistic model the data separate (a Firth-penalized fit with profile intervals and no Wald covariance), several tests are validly computed as the penalized likelihood-ratio test 2(l*(β̂) − max_{β_idx=0} l*(β)) on χ²(q): the spline's test of association, its nonlinearity test, and the quintile and category global tests. The restricted fit keeps the full model's penalty ½log|I(β)| (Heinze & Schemper 2002).
regime: inference; yes/no outcome with separation (Firth table)
user_sees: "The test of association: Penalized likelihood-ratio test that all 3 terms of `x` are zero (... the restricted fit keeping the full model's penalty (Heinze & Schemper 2002)): χ²(3) = ..."
claimed_basis: Heinze & Schemper 2002; "as logistf's nested tests are" (docstring); contract relation separation-plr (:2569)
notes: The R reference writes out the same penalized-LR formula (and checks the free fit against brglm2), so it checks that the code computes the formula. The χ²(q) calibration, and the choice of penalty for the restricted model, are not tested.

statement: Under multiple imputation, the spline's overall and nonlinearity tests and the quintile and category global tests are validly pooled by D1 (Li, Raghunathan & Rubin 1991). Knots and companion quintile cut points are placed once on the observed values and held fixed across copies, so every copy estimates coefficients of one variable.
regime: inference; multiple imputation with a declared form
decision: pooling of form tests across imputed copies
user_sees: "Pooled over 20 imputations by Li, Raghunathan & Rubin's D1 ..."
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 corrected ("form tests (D1)"); §1 row 5 ("fixed across imputations")
notes: Software reference (mitml D1). The pooling code is in turbotab/core/stages/modeling.py:_pool_form_tests (outside this slice). Fixed knots: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_ms1_ms3_multiple_imputation.py::test_4_knots_are_placed_once_on_observed_values_and_held_in_every_copy (behavior). _companion docstring is at :1890.

statement: When imputed copies give χ² statistics but no covariance (a Firth penalized LR test under separation), pooling them by D2 (Li, Meng, Raghunathan & Rubin 1991) gives a usable pooled test. D2 uses r₂ = (1+1/m)var(√dₘ) and D₂ = (d̄/k − (m+1)/(m−1)·r₂)/(1+r₂) on F(k, ν₂), with ν₂ = k^(−3/m)(m−1)(1+1/r₂)². When r₂ ≈ 0, D₂·k is referred to χ²(k).
regime: inference; multiple imputation and separation
decision: pooling of penalized LR form tests
user_sees: "Pooled over 20 imputations by Li, Meng, Raghunathan & Rubin's D2 ..."
claimed_basis: Li, Meng, Raghunathan & Rubin 1991; van Buuren, Flexible Imputation of Missing Data 2nd ed. §5.3.4
notes: Software reference (mitml:::.D2), so the test checks that the code computes D2. D2's accuracy is known to be weaker than D1's; a referee should judge whether it suits penalized LR statistics. The r₂ ≈ 0 fallback is the app's. By contrast, the interaction module refuses separation under MI (see the separation+MI refusal entry).

statement: Under inference, a data-derived 'optimal' cut point (the minimum-p split) gives an estimate and p-value biased away from the null, with an interval too narrow (Altman & Royston 2006). It is therefore blocked and kept only as a recorded limitation. Cut points for categories must be declared from outside the data.
regime: inference; continuous exposure or confounder
decision: functional form of a continuous exposure or confounder (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5)
user_sees: "...its estimate and p-value are biased away from the null (Altman & Royston 2006: \"the use of a data-derived 'optimal' cutpoint leads to serious bias\")."
claimed_basis: Altman & Royston 2006 BMJ 332:1080; MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 2 and §4 (block and record)
notes: test_form_4::test_4_a_data_derived_cut_point_is_blocked_under_inference_and_found_as_by_hand checks the refusal and the min-p search, not the bias. Exits: spline, quintiles, declared cut points, keep with acknowledgment. Other locations: option :1082, caption :1814 ("its p-value and interval are too small"), cuts_needed refusal :2126. Under prediction it ranks lower instead.

statement: Under inference, a continuous confounder cut into three or fewer groups leaves serious residual confounding, because within each group it still varies with the exposure. It is therefore blocked and kept only as a recorded limitation. Four or more groups pass (ranked lower), and the exposure's own declared categories pass.
regime: inference; adjusted continuous confounder declared as categories with ≤ 2 cut points
decision: functional form of a continuous exposure or confounder (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5)
user_sees: "`age` could explain the link and is cut into 3 groups: within each group it still varies with what you study, so its confounding is only partly removed (Brenner & Blettner 1997: ...)"
claimed_basis: Brenner & Blettner 1997 Epidemiology 8:429 ("if the number of categories is small"); MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 2 and §4
notes: test_form_4::test_4_a_confounder_in_three_or_fewer_groups_is_blocked_and_recorded is refusal-only. The ≤ 3 threshold is the ruling's; the source says only "small".

statement: Under inference, every adjusted confounder that is a numeric amount with at least 10 distinct values needs a declared functional form, and a restricted cubic spline is proposed, because a straight line that misses a curve leaves residual confounding. A numeric covariate with fewer than 10 distinct values may enter as recorded (a straight line) without a declared form.

claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5 ("Continuous confounders get a declared form too"); the 10-value threshold: none stated
notes: test_form_4::test_4_the_form_question_asks_each_continuous_confounder_and_proposes_a_spline is behavior. CONTINUOUS = 10 is at :105.

statement: For an exposure on its raw scale with no negative values and at least 5% of values exactly zero, the soundest form models non-consumers as their own reference category. Beside that indicator it fits a restricted cubic spline among consumers, with knots at consumers' percentiles. This is the proposal and leads the options.

Other locations: option :1093, proposal :1334. statement: For the mass-at-zero form, the test of association is the joint Wald test that the consumer indicator and every spline term are zero (k df). Nonlinearity among consumers is tested on the k−2 nonlinear terms alone. This works because every spline column is zero at zero intake, with all knots above zero.
regime: inference; zero_spline form
user_sees: "Wald test that the 2 nonlinear terms of `fish_g` among consumers are zero ..."
claimed_basis: none stated beyond docstrings (:600, :1680)
notes: The NumPy reference builds the same design, so it checks that the code computes the test. It also asserts the basis is 0 at x = 0.

statement: Restricting the analysis to consumers (exposure > 0) changes the estimand to the effect among consumers rather than in the whole population. It is therefore recorded as an estimand change (STROBE-nut nut-14), offered only under inference and only for the declared exposure. It is refused under prediction because the model is applied to everyone.
regime: inference (refused under prediction); declared exposure with zeros
user_sees: "A consumers-only domain changes the population the estimate is about; under prediction the model is used on everyone, consumers or not."
claimed_basis: STROBE-nut (Lachat et al. 2016) nut-14; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 2 and §2 ("Zeros in a food exposure")

statement: A domain transform of the exposure invalidates a previously declared functional form, its knots, its cut points and the estimand's unit. Such transforms are a log, an energy residual or density, scale scoring, omics normalization and batch adjustment. The form must be re-asked on the new scale rather than kept.
regime: inference (and any declared form); exposure transformed after its form was declared

No further confounder adjustment for M is needed, because effect modification concerns one intervention's effect varying across strata of M (VanderWeele 2009).

statement: On a ratio scale, additive interaction is RERI = RR₁₁ − RR₁₀ − RR₀₁ + 1, computed from the model's exponentiated contrasts. Its 95% interval is the symmetric Wald interval from the delta-method variance gᵀVg, with g = e^{L₁₁}c₁₁ − e^{L₁₀}c₁₀ − e^{L₀₁}c₀₁ (Hosmer & Lemeshow 1992). The reference is z, or t on the combination df.
regime: inference; odds-, hazard- or cumulative-odds-ratio model with product terms
decision: additive interaction measure and its interval

statement: The reference distribution for a linear combination of coefficients (a stratum effect, a joint effect, a ratio of ratios, a RERI) depends on the covariance. It is t on n−p under HC3, t on the design df under a survey, and normal for a model-based table.

statement: The gap statistic is a sound rule for k that can answer 'no subgroups'. It uses squared Euclidean distances and reference data drawn uniformly in the box of the data's principal components (Tibshirani et al.'s reference (b)). It chooses the smallest k with Gap(k) ≥ Gap(k+1) − s(k+1), where s = √(1+1/B)·sd, or the largest k searched when none qualifies.

claimed_basis: Tibshirani, Walther & Hastie 2001; cluster::clusGap(spaceH0 = scaledPCA, d.power = 2); cluster::maxSE(Tibs2001SEmax)
notes: Software references (clusGap, maxSE, test_the_gap_rule_is_maxse_tibs2001) and a by-hand rule test: they check computation, not the rule's soundness. tibs_se_max is at :546.

statement: For mixed numeric and categorical columns, a sound way to find subgroups is k-medoids (PAM, BUILD then SWAP) on the Gower dissimilarity, with k by the average silhouette width. The Gower dissimilarity averages, over columns, |difference|/range for numbers, rank difference/range for ordered categories, and a 0/1 mismatch for unordered categories.

statement: A subgroup's stability is its mean bootstrap Jaccard similarity with the most similar subgroup re-found on each resample's distinct people (Hennig 2007, as fpc::clusterboot computes it). A mean of 0.5 or less means the subgroup dissolves; above 0.75 means it is recovered. Under an unweighted design, whole PSUs are resampled within strata.
regime: cluster analysis with k ≥ 2 and n_boot > 0

notes: Software reference; also test_kmeans_stability_agrees_with_clusterboot (within MC error). PSU-within-strata resampling for an unweighted design (resamples :591) has only a behavior test (test_weighted_kmeans_resamples_psus_within_strata).

statement: With survey weights, design-based k-means weights each person in three places, each invariant to rescaling all weights and equal to the unweighted version under equal weights. The standardization uses the weighted mean and svyvar's SD Σw(x−m)²/Σw·n/(n−1). The within-subgroup sum of squares is weighted. The silhouette's a is the weighted mean distance to the others in the subgroup and b the weighted mean distance to another subgroup; WeightedCluster's ASW and ASWw are not scale-invariant in this way.
regime: k-means with the silhouette rule under survey weights
user_sees: "Survey weights entered the standardization (the design-based standard deviation; Lumley 2004 ...), the k-means objective and the silhouette, each unchanged by the weights' scale."
claimed_basis: Lumley 2004 (survey::svyvar); Studer 2013 (WeightedCluster) as contrast; contract relation weighted_kmeans (:1278)
notes: The R reference (svymean/svyvar; kmeans on rows repeated by integer weights; weighted silhouette written out in R) checks computation. That this silhouette is the right design-based quantity is the app's definition. Also test_multiplying_every_weight_by_one_constant_changes_nothing and test_the_weighted_silhouette_by_hand. standardize is at :290.

statement: Under survey weights, stability uses the Rao–Wu–Yue (1992) rescaled bootstrap. In each stratum of n_h PSUs, n_h−1 PSUs are drawn with replacement and a drawn PSU's weights are multiplied by n_h/(n_h−1)×(times drawn); a one-PSU stratum keeps its weight. The replicate variance of a weighted total matches the with-replacement design variance, and the Jaccard is counted in weights.

notes: A known-truth comparison against survey::svytotal's variance (within 8%). That this validates the Jaccard stability is not tested. A lone-PSU stratum contributes no variance.
