notes: test_an_exposure_on_another_scale_and_a_category_exposure_are_refused is refusal-only.

statement: An exposure that the fit splits into one coefficient per level cannot be followed on a single-number curve, so a categorical exposure is refused.
regime: Estimate; categorical exposure
decision: exposure type allowed on the curve
user_sees: "`g` is a category, so the fit would give one coefficient per level; the curve follows one number per specification."
claimed_basis: none stated

statement: An option that drops the exposure is invalid: the exposure is fitted in every specification, so that option would be the primary again under another name.
regime: Estimate; an option whose drop list names the exposure
user_sees: "“without the exposure” drops `x`, the column every specification studies, so it would stay in and this would be the primary again under another name."
claimed_basis: none stated
notes: This is a logic claim with little methods content.

statement: The specification curve is not offered under Predict, because choices there are made inside each training fold and compared by cross-validated scores, leaving no single estimate to follow. It is not offered under Describe, because no model of the exposure is fit.
regime: Predict or Describe goal
user_sees: "Under Predict the choices are made inside each training fold and compared by their scores, so there is no single estimate to follow across them."
claimed_basis: contract relation predict_refused (:681)
notes: test_the_curve_is_offered_under_estimate_only is refusal-only.

statement: Under inference, multiple imputation of missing predictors with the outcome and total energy in the imputation model, pooled by Rubin's rules, gives unbiased regression coefficients and intervals with nominal coverage when the blanks are missing at random given the imputation-model variables.
regime: inference purpose; any outcome type with missing predictor values; MAR given the imputation-model variables
decision: missing-values method (set_missing): ranked first and recommended under inference
user_sees: Sound: with the outcome and energy in the imputation model it is unbiased under missing at random and its intervals carry the imputation's uncertainty (Moons et al. 2006).
claimed_basis: Moons et al. 2006; Harrell RMS §3.8; Sterne et al. 2009; BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 4; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 6
notes: Partial: one linear-outcome simulation (confounder ~40% MAR given the exposure, n = 1000, 400 reps; |bias| < 0.01, coverage >= 0.93). Not tested for binary/Cox outcomes or for the 'energy in the model' part. Same rule in RULE (missing.py:69-74), imputation.py:3-10, contract leash missing.py:1893. Doc: BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 4 (Moons 2006; Sterne 2009; Sisk 2023), the prediction half in S3-002/S3-003.

statement: Under prediction, multiple imputation that uses the outcome is invalid because a held-out row's own outcome would fill its predictors and a new row at deployment has no outcome, so imputation must instead be fit within each training fold without the outcome.
regime: prediction or undeclared purpose; any task; missing predictors
decision: set_missing: multiple imputation refused under prediction
user_sees: Not here: it uses the outcome, which a new row does not have; impute in each fold without it (Sisk et al. 2023).
claimed_basis: Sisk et al. 2023; BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 4
notes: Refusal raised in turbotab/core/decisions.py:4829-4841 (code imputation_with_the_outcome); rung 'refused' at missing.py:133. test_wp7::test_1_multiple_imputation_with_the_outcome_is_refused_under_prediction only checks that the refusal fires. The app's own Sisk quote (missing.py:31-33) says the outcome SHOULD be used to impute development data under MI when data are complete at deployment; the refusal applies regardless of whether missingness is allowed at deployment. Doc: BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 4 (supersedes the lockbox constitution §07 'never').

statement: Under prediction, a single fill learned on each training fold without the outcome (median for numbers, most frequent value for categories and yes/no columns) is the sound and recommended way to handle missing predictors, because the fitted pipeline then imputes a new row exactly as it was developed.
regime: prediction (or undeclared purpose); any task; predictors with blanks that do not mean 'not asked'
decision: set_missing ranking and recommended fill under prediction
user_sees: Sound: fit in each training fold without the outcome, it imputes a new row as it was developed (Josse et al. 2019; Sisk et al. 2023).
claimed_basis: Josse et al. 2019; Sisk et al. 2023; BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 4; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1.1 (prediction step 1)
notes: recommended_fills (missing.py:251-270) picks median vs most frequent; RULE missing.py:69-74. test_wp7::test_2_* only check reproducibility against scikit-learn (code computes F), not predictive merit versus alternatives (indicators, outcome-free MI).

statement: Complete-case analysis gives unbiased regression coefficients if and only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors.
regime: inference; complete-case analysis of a regression (linear, logistic, Cox, etc.) with missing predictors
decision: complete-cases option (available, ranked second under inference); its stated assumption in the record and methods sentence; the row-loss concern
user_sees: complete cases give unbiased coefficients only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors (Groenwold et al. 2012; White & Carlin 2010)
claimed_basis: Groenwold et al. 2012; White & Carlin 2010
notes: Partial: the complete-case arm checks only the sufficiency direction in one linear scenario (missingness depends on the exposure). The option label (missing.py:139) says 'Sound if ...' (sufficient) while COMPLETE_CASE_ASSUMPTION and row_loss_concern (missing.py:1763-1764: 'estimate without bias only if') assert necessity; for logistic-regression odds ratios complete cases are also unbiased when missingness depends on the outcome alone, so 'only if' may be overstated for binary outcomes.

statement: Under inference, losing more than 10% of the rows to complete-case analysis is enough to warrant a concern, shown with a comparison of the kept and dropped rows' outcome and predictors.
regime: inference; complete-case strategy; share of rows dropped > 0.10
decision: concern on the fit (complete-case row loss)
user_sees: Complete cases drop N of M rows (x%), more than the 10% at which CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK flags listwise deletion. ... multiple imputation keeps every row.
claimed_basis: CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK anti-pattern 1 ('Flag when listwise deletion drops >10% of rows')
notes: ROW_LOSS_SHARE at missing.py:87. test_wp7::test_7_* check the threshold and the pooled-SD SMD arithmetic only. The kept-vs-dropped comparison can only reveal dependence on observed variables.

statement: Under inference, a single (median or most-frequent) fill gives intervals that are too narrow because imputed values are treated as measured, and biases a coefficient whenever who is missing depends on another variable, so it is blocked unless recorded as a limitation.
regime: inference; any outcome; missing predictors filled once (median, most frequent, energy-aware line)
decision: set_missing single fill under inference: block and record; holds the inference table
user_sees: Under inference a single fill is blocked until it is recorded: a single fill treats each imputed value as measured, so the intervals are too narrow, and a median fill biases a coefficient ...
claimed_basis: audit ME-01 (median fill bias +38-75%, coverage 0.00); MODELING_SEQUENCE §4 ('Median fill: block and record for the inference table')
notes: Median arm of the test: bias > 0.15 and coverage < 0.05 in one MAR-given-exposure scenario; the general 'whenever' is not tested. Rung at missing.py:151; table hold missing.py:760; refusal decisions.py:4876-4883 ('single_fill_under_inference').

statement: In a nonrandomized study the missing-indicator method (a missing indicator, or blanks as their own category) almost always biases the estimates, whereas for baseline covariates in a randomized trial it is valid.
regime: inference; observational study vs randomized trial; missing covariates
decision: set_missing with indicators or blanks-as-level under inference: block and record (exit names the RCT/not-asked exception)
user_sees: Under inference the missing-indicator method is blocked until it is recorded: the missing-indicator method almost always biases the estimates of a nonrandomized study (Groenwold et al. 2012); ...
claimed_basis: Groenwold et al. 2012 (CMAJ 184:1265)
notes: Rungs missing.py:159 and 168; missing_block missing.py:750-759; refusal decisions.py:4864-4872 with exit 'a blank here means not asked, or the covariates are baseline ones in a randomized trial'. Tests only check the refusal fires.

statement: When a yes/no column's blank means the question was not asked (a skip pattern), a most-frequent fill gives those rows the commonest answer among people who were asked, an answer nobody gave, so under prediction keeping those blanks as their own level is the recommended fill.
regime: prediction (or undeclared purpose); yes/no or categorical predictors flagged likely_not_asked
decision: ranking of fills and the default completion of an unsaid categorical fill
user_sees: Sound: blank in `meds_hbp` means not asked, so the blank is a value of its own; the other blanks are filled in each training fold.
claimed_basis: WALKABLE_PLAN §1 blocker B5 (NHANES meds_hbp: 15,552 never asked)
notes: NOT_ASKED_CAUTION missing.py:199-200; default completion missing.py:415-423 silently sets categorical=missing_category when unsaid. turbotab/core/tests/test_skip_pattern_blanks.py checks behavior on NHANES, not predictive merit.

statement: Under inference, when a column's blanks mean the question was not asked, treating the blank as its own level is sound because the missing-indicator bias (a value that exists but is unseen) does not arise, whereas multiple imputation would give those rows an answer drawn from the people who were asked, an answer nobody gave.
regime: inference; not-asked yes/no columns (blanks-as-level first only when they are the only predictors with blanks)
decision: ranking under inference; honest default set with an attestation
user_sees: Sound here: blank in `x` means not asked, so the blank is a value, not a missing one, and the missing-indicator bias (a value that exists, unseen) does not arise; recorded with that reason.
claimed_basis: none stated beyond the Groenwold mechanism; NOT_ASKED_MI_CAUTION missing.py:311-312
notes: honest_default missing.py:273-287. The not-asked level is usually determined by a gating answer (e.g. 'never told high BP'), so it is collinear with that covariate; referee may check what its coefficient estimates.

statement: A yes/no (one- or two-valued) or medication column that is blank on at least half the rows with the outcome measured has blanks that mean 'not asked' (a skip pattern) rather than values missing at random.
regime: any purpose; yes/no or medication-named predictors
decision: which fill is recommended or completed by default
user_sees: A yes/no medication question blank on `x%` of rows: blank usually means not asked.
claimed_basis: WALKABLE_PLAN §1 blocker B5 (NHANES meds_hbp); no general source
notes: Threshold NOT_ASKED_SHARE = 0.5 in turbotab/core/stages/proposals.py:61, flag at proposals.py:1145, text at proposals.py:1114. Docstring missing.py:243-244: random blanks on a quarter of rows are not a skip pattern. A heuristic: a high blank share alone does not establish a skip pattern.

statement: A single fill of an energy-bearing nutrient by its median makes the imputed rows' energy-adjusted (residual) values correlate -1 with energy, whereas filling each blank from the nutrient's in-fold least-squares line on total energy preserves the nutrient-energy relation that the residual method depends on.
regime: single fill (prediction, or attested under inference); energy-bearing nutrient exposures with a numeric total-energy column
decision: how a single fill imputes nutrients
user_sees: ...the median for numbers, most frequent value for categories ... line on total energy (kcal) ... without the outcome
claimed_basis: audit D11 (median fill: -1.000 against +0.78 for observed rows)
notes: energy_fill missing.py:492-512; docstring missing.py:37-41. The test shows the median gives -1 and the line fill gives adjusted values uncorrelated with energy; it does not test bias of a downstream coefficient. Fills are clipped to the observed range (missing.py:602); a row missing energy too reads energy at its median.

statement: For a left-censored predictor in a linear model, replacing each non-detect by its expected value below the detection limit under a censored-normal (Tobit) fit to the column, on the raw or log scale, leaves the slope approximately unbiased by the regression-calibration argument E[X*E[X|W]] = E[E[X|W]^2].
regime: prediction, in-fold and outcome-free; columns named by the left-censoring finding or recoded zeros
decision: below-detection answer: censoring-aware ranked first and recommended
user_sees: Sound for associations. Each non-detect becomes its expected value below the limit under a censored-normal fit, in each training fold without the outcome.
claimed_basis: regression-calibration argument (docstring); Lubin et al. 2004; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1.1 prediction step 3
notes: Partial: one-covariate simulation (log-intensity N(10,1), 60% censored, 200 reps), prediction arm within 5% of 0.5. The docstring's regime is 'one censored covariate', but the fill E[X|X<L] conditions only on censoring, not on other covariates, so with correlated covariates it is not E[X|W] and the argument may fail; the app applies it with any covariates. The fill value matches R survreg in turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_ms7_omics.py::test_4e_the_censoring_aware_fill_is_the_expected_value_below_the_limit_under_rs_tobit_fit (code computes F). below_detection_options missing.py:441-452.

statement: Under inference, drawing each non-detect within the multiple imputation from a censored-normal (Tobit) model truncated at the detection limit, conditional on the outcome, gives unbiased association estimates and nominal confidence intervals unless the share below the limit is extreme.
regime: inference; left-censored predictors under multiple imputation
decision: below-detection answer under inference: censoring-aware recommended
user_sees: Sound for associations. A censored-normal (Tobit) draw below the limit within the multiple imputation, given the outcome (Lubin et al. 2004).
claimed_basis: Lubin et al. 2004 (quoted); MODELING_SEQUENCE §1.1 inference step 1 ('detection-limit blanks use the censored model, never MAR')
notes: Partial: one scenario (60% censored), inference arm within 5% and coverage >= 0.92. Draw at imputation.py:401-414. Under SMC-FCS mode a censored variable is not drawn from a Tobit fit: its covariate model is a normal regression on all rows' current values, truncated at the limit, with rejection on the outcome density (smcfcs.py:414, 845-846, 516-517).

statement: Substituting half the smallest detected value for non-detects biases association estimates increasingly as the censored share grows, and is acceptable (customary) only when roughly 10% or fewer of values lie below the limit.
regime: left-censored predictors (metabolomics and similar), either purpose
decision: below-detection ranking: half-minimum 'available', below censoring-aware; its label above 10% censored
user_sees: Biased for associations as censoring grows, and collapses every non-detect to one value (Lubin et al. 2004: biased unless 5–10% are below the limit).
claimed_basis: Lubin et al. 2004; MetaboAnalyst's default (customary); MODELING_SEQUENCE §1.1 ('half-minimum is customary at <= 10% censored')
notes: Partial: the half-minimum arm averages < 0.3 (truth 0.5) at 60% censored; acceptability at <= 10% is not tested. CENSORED_CUSTOMARY_MAX = 0.10 in turbotab/core/methods/omics.py:1113; label 'customary only to 10%' in decisions.py:4997-4999. Label says '5–10%', threshold is 10%.

statement: Filling non-detects with the column median, as ordinary missing values, places known-small values in the middle of the distribution and biases associations, so such a fill is refused (under prediction kept only with a stated reason).
regime: columns holding values below a detection limit; either purpose
decision: set_missing without a below-detection answer: refused (as_missing rung 'refused')
user_sees: Unsound: the median places non-detections in the middle of the distribution.
claimed_basis: audit ME-08
notes: Partial: median arm averages > 0.6 (truth 0.5) at 60% censored. Docstring missing.py:43-50; refusal decisions.py:4970-5027 ('median_below_detection').

statement: Under inference, multiple imputation that treats non-detects as missing at random is invalid because each blank is known to lie below the limit, so it is refused whatever reason is given and a censoring-aware draw is required.
regime: inference; left-censored predictors; strategy multiple imputation without a below-detection answer
decision: set_missing refused under inference even with a reason
user_sees: ... each blank is known to be small, but multiple imputation reads them as missing at random. Choose how non-detections are filled; under inference they are never filled as missing at random.
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §4 ('MAR imputation of detection-limit blanks: refuse, censoring-aware instead') and §2
notes: Enforced in decisions.py (likely another slice; merge if duplicated); the options it offers come from missing.py:441-462. test_wp7::test_6_median_fill_of_non_detections_is_refused_unless_given_a_reason only checks the refusal; no test runs MAR MI on non-detects. Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (New) 'Detection-limit readings imply censoring-aware handling; MAR imputation of those blanks is refused under inference'.

statement: For a left-censored column, modeling it on the log scale only when a censored normal on log x raises the Jacobian-corrected maximized log-likelihood by more than 2 over the raw scale chooses the right scale for the censoring-aware fill or draw; wrongly assuming the log scale for already-logged values biases the pooled slope (11% high at 60% censored).
regime: left-censored columns under the censoring-aware answer, either purpose
decision: scale of the Tobit model for a censored column
user_sees: nothing directly; the censoring-aware fill or draw changes
claimed_basis: audit simulation (0.557 vs 0.5; raw scale 0.513); 'over 100 draws of 300 rows' selection check stated in the docstring
notes: log_scale_fits_better imputation.py:177-189; LOG_GAIN = 2.0 at imputation.py:81 (LR > e^2). No test of the stated selection property; test_wp7::test_6 implicitly needs the raw-scale choice for N(10,1) values (partial).

statement: Under inference, passive multiple imputation (each variable drawn from a model linear in it, with declared nonlinear terms such as splines, quintiles, a log residual or a density derived afterwards in each copy) biases the curvature and the nonlinearity tests toward the null, so it is blocked unless recorded.
regime: inference; multiple imputation with a declared nonlinear/derived term; also ordinal/multinomial outcomes where no SMC-FCS is built
decision: set_missing imputation_model 'passive': block and record; holds the table
user_sees: Under inference passive multiple imputation with a restricted cubic spline of `x` is blocked until it is recorded: passive imputation draws each value from a model linear in it ...
claimed_basis: Bartlett et al. 2015 (Table 2: passive 0.696, SMC-FCS 0.998); MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 5, §4
notes: Test covers a quadratic term with a linear outcome (passive ~0.70, coverage <= 5%); not splines, quintiles, log residuals, densities or binary/Cox outcomes, and 'tests biased toward the null' is not tested directly. missing_block missing.py:732-742; nonlinear_terms missing.py:769-794 decides which terms count; contract missing.py:1895-1920; refusal decisions.py:4908-4925. Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 5 (critical finding of the 2026-10-03 review).

statement: Multiple imputation is compatible with the analysis model only if it is SMC-FCS whenever the outcome is binary or time-to-event or the analysis model holds a term nonlinear in an imputed variable (spline, quintiles, log, ratio), while for a linear outcome model linear in the imputed variables chained equations with the outcome as a predictor are compatible.
regime: inference; multiple imputation; linear, logistic or Cox analysis models
decision: imputation mode (SMC-FCS vs chained equations) chosen by default
user_sees: Missing values were multiply imputed by substantive-model-compatible fully conditional specification (SMC-FCS; Bartlett et al. 2015), compatible with the analysis model, a linear model with ...
claimed_basis: Bartlett et al. 2015; Seaman, Bartlett & White 2012; MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 5, §1.1, §2
notes: Partial; the 'FCS is compatible for linear' half is exercised by test_wp7::test_1_multiple_imputation_is_unbiased_and_its_intervals_cover. Docstrings missing.py:1281-1286 and smcfcs.py:4-19; contract option missing.py:1819-1825; relation 'a change to the form or energy model invalidates the imputations' missing.py:1859-1863.

statement: For an ordinal outcome (entered as its codes as one numeric term) or a multinomial outcome (entered as class indicators), chained equations with the outcome in the imputation model are compatible with the analysis model when it has no nonlinear term.
regime: inference; ordinal or multiclass outcome; multiple imputation with no declared nonlinear term
decision: imputation mode and the record's 'compatible' flag and methods sentence
user_sees: Missing values were multiply imputed by chained equations with the outcome in the imputation model, compatible with the analysis model, linear in the imputed variables
claimed_basis: none stated (docstring missing.py:1283-1285: 'no SMC-FCS for them here')
notes: SUBSTANTIVE (missing.py:844) has no ordinal/multinomial entry, so compatible = (smc or not nonlinear) is True; outcome_terms imputation.py:192-212; sentence missing.py:1574-1576. For a binary outcome under the passive answer the app labels the same kind of chained equations 'only approximately' compatible (missing.py:1564-1569); ordinal/multinomial are not labeled approximate. Entering ordered codes as one linear term restricts X|Y to be linear in the code.

statement: The engine's SMC-FCS sampler (the outcome never a covariate-model predictor; covariate and substantive model parameters drawn each update; binary and categorical variables drawn directly from p(x|z)f(y|x,z); continuous ones by rejection sampling with acceptance f(y|x*,z)/max f, Cox using the Efron-tie baseline hazard at the drawn coefficients; up to 1,024 candidates, a failure keeping its last) reproduces Bartlett et al.'s algorithm as R smcfcs 2.0.2 implements it.
regime: inference; SMC-FCS for linear, logistic and Cox substantive models
decision: how the imputed copies are drawn
user_sees: SMC-FCS kept no candidate for N draws within its limit of 1,000 candidates each; those values kept their last candidate, as R's smcfcs does.
claimed_basis: Bartlett et al. 2015; R smcfcs 2.0.2 source (smcfcs:::smcfcs.core); survival::basehaz
notes: Also MS::test_1_smcfcs_cox_spline_agrees_with_r_smcfcs and MS::test_1_smcfcs_logistic_product_term_agrees_with_r_smcfcs (pooled estimates within 2 MC SE jointly, m = 50) and test_mi_repair.py::test_8_the_cox_draws_baseline_hazard_is_basehaz_of_the_efron_fit_at_the_draw (to 1e-10); R tests skip without Rscript. outcome_logdensity smcfcs.py:310-324; _reject 898-943; _cox_draw 282-293; failure concern missing.py:1681-1684.

statement: A variable the analysis takes the log of (nutrients and energy in a log-residual or density model, quotient-normalized columns) should be imputed on the log scale (modeled and drawn as log x, returned as exp), which keeps every copy positive and the imputation compatible with the analysis model.
regime: inference; multiple imputation with logged analysis terms
decision: scale on which incomplete columns are imputed
user_sees: ; `fiber_g` and `protein_g` were imputed on the log scale, as the analysis takes their log
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §1.1 ('logged quantities are imputed on the log scale')
notes: Partial: the test checks positivity and the record only, not unbiasedness. smcfcs.py:42-43; relation missing.py:1845-1848. Sits beside imputation.py:33-38 (von Hippel: impute skewed variables untransformed) — the app logs only what the analysis logs.

statement: A recorded zero in a column the analysis logs is a detection-limit question, not missing data, so it must never be imputed or median-filled, and the imputation is refused until that question is answered.
regime: inference multiple imputation (and every stage fitting completed copies); logged columns with zeros
decision: imputation refused; copies' impute step refuses blanks made inside a copy
user_sees: `x` is analyzed on the log scale and is zero or negative on N rows, so it cannot be imputed on that scale; a zero a log would turn into a blank goes to the detection-limit question, never to a fill.
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §1.1 ('A zero that a log would turn missing is sent to the detection-limit question, never to median fill')
notes: CopyGuard missing.py:951-978. MS::test_2_a_recorded_zero_in_a_logged_column_is_refused_* check the refusal only. A zero may be a true zero (a non-consumer) rather than a non-detect; MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 routes food zeros to a two-part exposure instead.

statement: When total energy is the sum of energy sources with settled kcal-per-unit factors plus other energy, imputing the sources and 'other' (truncated so other stays >= 0) and deriving total energy as their sum keeps E = sum(f_j N_j) + other with other non-negative in every copy, which imputing total energy as its own variable would not.
regime: inference; multiple imputation under an energy adjustment whose nutrients have settled kcal-per-unit factors
decision: which energy variables are imputed and which derived
user_sees: ; the energy sources (`protein_g`, `fat_g` and `carb_g`) and the rest of energy were imputed and total energy (`kcal`) derived as their sum, so the rest is never negative
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §1.1
notes: Tests verify the identity property (also test_mi_repair::test_3_two_blank_sources_under_a_recorded_total_never_take_the_rest_below_zero), not unbiasedness of downstream estimates. smcfcs.py:44-60; relation missing.py:1849-1854. Infeasible rows are counted and raised (missing.py:1685-1692); the feasible start (START_SHARE = 0.5) is a heuristic.

statement: When imputing an energy source under the energy identity, its covariate model should condition on the recorded total energy rather than on 'other' (which on a row with a recorded total is a function of the source itself); conditioning on 'other' holds each draw near its previous value and biases the imputed sources.
regime: inference; multiple imputation with the energy identity, total energy recorded on some rows
decision: predictors of an energy source's covariate model
user_sees: nothing directly; the imputed sources change
claimed_basis: the MI repair's simulation (with other: -4 to -5.5 SE low; with the total: within +/-1.4 SE)
notes: 3 seeds x 4 configurations within 3 simulation SE, with a control arm (other as predictor) that must fall below -3 SE. Only the imputed source means are checked, not downstream coefficients or variances. Docstring smcfcs.py:56-60.

statement: Under multiple imputation, spline knots and quintile or category cut points must be placed once on the observed values (Harrell's percentiles) and held identical in every completed copy, so that Rubin's rules pool coefficients of one common basis.
regime: inference; multiple imputation with spline, quintile, zero-spline or category forms
decision: knots and cut points used by every stage fitting the copies
user_sees: ; the knots of `x` (...) were placed once on its observed values and held in every copy
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 step 5; wave-1 verification (35 knot sets over 35 copies pooled as one basis)
notes: FixedForms missing.py:925-948; copy_pipeline missing.py:1003-1014; relation missing.py:1855-1858. MS::test_4_* and test_mi_repair::test_4_* verify identical knots (code property). Knots on observed values only can sit away from the full-data quantiles when missingness depends on x's predictors; a quintile's trend score stays per copy; data-derived 'optimal' cut points are skipped under imputation (missing.py:915).

statement: Under a survey design, including the strata, PSU-within-stratum and the weight as predictors in every covariate imputation model is the safest specification for a design-based analysis of the imputed data.
regime: inference; multiple imputation with a survey design (population estimand)
user_sees: ; the survey strata (`SDMVSTRA`), PSU (`SDMVPSU`) and weight (`WTMEC2YR`) were in the imputation model: in each covariate model and, beside the analysis model's terms, in its outcome model
claimed_basis: Reiter, Raghunathan & Kinney 2006 (quoted); MODELING_SEQUENCE §2
notes: MS::test_5_the_imputation_model_holds_the_strata_psu_and_weight checks presence only. Unplaced rows get a level of their own and the median weight (missing.py:1086-1099); PSU enters as within-stratum labels (indicators). Relation missing.py:1864-1870. Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (New) 'Survey design with a population estimand implies design variables in the imputation model, and ν_com = the design df' (the df half is S3-029).

statement: Because SMC-FCS assumes an auxiliary variable of the covariate models is conditionally independent of the outcome given the substantive model's covariates, the survey design's strata, PSU and weight must also enter the substantive (outcome) model; with them only in the covariate models, an outcome that differs by stratum biases the pooled design-based estimates.
regime: inference; SMC-FCS with a survey design
decision: terms of the SMC-FCS substantive model
user_sees: ...: in each covariate model and, beside the analysis model's terms, in its outcome model
claimed_basis: Bartlett et al. 2015 §5.3; smcfcs documentation; Meng 1994; Reiter, Raghunathan & Kinney 2006; MS2 repair simulation (z -0.06, ~7 MC SE)
notes: 24 replicates, linear outcome, 3-knot spline, with a control arm that must show z's bias. Not tested for logistic/Cox substantive models. _DesignTerms missing.py:1127-1180; smcfcs.py:72-77.

statement: Under a survey design, the complete-data degrees of freedom used in Barnard-Rubin's df and in D1's denominator df is the design's degrees of freedom (number of PSUs minus number of strata).
regime: inference; multiple imputation with a design-based (Taylor-linearized) analysis
decision: nu_com in Rubin's rules and D1
user_sees: ; the estimates were pooled by Rubin's rules, multi-parameter tests by D1 (Li, Raghunathan & Rubin 1991), on the design's 8 degrees of freedom

notes: The R test uses the same convention, so it checks the computation given it ('F is the estimator'); also MS::test_8_d1_on_the_design_df_takes_reiters_denominator_df_as_mitml_does. _design_df in turbotab/core/stages/modeling.py:1611-1621; sentence missing.py:1611-1612. statement: Outside a survey design, each pooled coefficient's complete-data degrees of freedom in Barnard-Rubin's formula is the mean over copies of that row's own reference df (n - p for HC3 rows, the Bell-McCaffrey df for CR2 rows), and is infinite (Rubin's 1987 nu_old) for rows on a normal reference.
regime: inference; multiple imputation; HC3, CR2 or Wald-z coefficient tables
decision: pooled df and interval of each coefficient
user_sees: Multiple imputation, m = 20: each completed table analyzed as follows, then pooled by Rubin's rules, each interval on t with Barnard–Rubin degrees of freedom.
claimed_basis: Barnard & Rubin 1999 (docstring imputation.py:56-58: 'nu_com each table's own complete-data degrees of freedom')
notes: The test covers only the HC3 case (nu_com = n - 3). Untested for CR2 rows, where the Satterthwaite (Bell-McCaffrey) df differs across copies and is averaged; whether a Satterthwaite df is a valid nu_com in Barnard-Rubin is not established in the repo. Logistic/multinomial Wald rows get nu_com = infinity, so their reference is t(nu_old).

statement: Pooling the m copies' estimates by Rubin's rules (mean estimate, total variance T = U + (1 + 1/m)B) with a t reference on Barnard & Rubin's (1999) degrees of freedom, and taking gamma = (r + 2/(nu + 3))/(1 + r) as the fraction of missing information, gives valid pooled intervals and p-values.
regime: inference; multiple imputation (engine's copies or the data's own)
user_sees: Multiple imputation, m = 20: each completed table analyzed as follows, then pooled by Rubin's rules, each interval on t with Barnard–Rubin degrees of freedom.
claimed_basis: Rubin 1987; Barnard & Rubin 1999; van Buuren 2018 §2.3 eq. 2.16-2.32
notes: By-formula test, plus R mice::pool.scalar in MS::test_5_pooled_coefficients_and_intervals_agree_with_r_survey_and_mitools and MS::test_10_the_pooled_table_agrees_with_r_mitools ('F is the estimator'); validity only via test_wp7::test_1_multiple_imputation_is_unbiased_and_its_intervals_cover. Engine follows Barnard-Rubin's 1 - lambda (as mice), not MIcombine's U/(U+B). pool_scalar imputation.py:543-562; docstring 53-61.

statement: Multi-parameter tests under multiple imputation (spline overall and nonlinearity, global quintile, interaction) are validly pooled by Li, Raghunathan & Rubin's D1 on F(k, nu1), with nu1 = 4 + (t - 4)[1 + (1 - 2/t)/r1]^2 for t = k(m - 1) > 4 (else t(1 + 1/k)(1 + 1/r1)^2/2), and with Reiter's (2007) small-sample denominator df when the complete-data df is finite.
regime: inference; multiple imputation; multi-df Wald tests
user_sees: ; the estimates were pooled by Rubin's rules, multi-parameter tests by D1 (Li, Raghunathan & Rubin 1991)

notes: Also MS::test_8_the_global_quintile_test_agrees_with_mitml_d1, test_8_an_interaction_test_agrees_with_mitml_d1, test_8_d1_on_the_design_df_takes_reiters_denominator_df_as_mitml_does, test_8_a_cox_splines_tests_are_pooled_by_d1_as_mitml_pools_them, and test_wp7::test_1_rubins_rules_and_d1_match_the_formulas — all against mitml or the formula ('F is the estimator'); no type-I simulation of D1. With r1 ~ 0 it falls to chi2_k; with a finite df_com and t <= 4 the small-t formula ignores df_com. reiter_df imputation.py:565-578.

statement: With rows clustered by unit, imputing confirmed time-invariant variables once per unit and imputing row-level variables with the unit means of the other row-level variables plus the variable's own mean over the unit's other rows preserves the intraclass correlation, an adequate approximation to two-level imputation.

statement: Under inference, when an identifier or cluster column the user confirmed repeats across the analysis rows, intervals that ignore the repetition are too narrow, so the coefficient table is made cluster-robust by that column even when the grain answer said one row per unit or 'don't know'.

decision: covariance type of the coefficient table

claimed_basis: Cameron & Miller 2015
notes: 1,000 reps of 300 people x 3 rows: coverage >= 0.93, plain OLS <= 0.88. Docstring inference.py:5-10. Among repeating identifiers the coarsest (fewest units) is chosen.

statement: When rows nest within units and units nest within a grouping the user named (e.g., a household above a person), intervals should cluster at the highest correlated level, the grouping above the unit.

claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 ('at the highest correlated level')

user_sees: `x` repeats (N values over M rows), and whether rows sharing it belong together is asked, not assumed ... Intervals that cluster by it, or that ignore it, would each rest on a guess.

statement: If the rows were said to repeat but no column identifies the unit, intervals that treat the rows as independent would be too narrow, so no interval is reported.

decision: no interval; exit to name the unit column

regime: inference; clustered rows with G < 8
decision: no interval or p-value; exits offered

statement: Below the cluster floor, for a continuous outcome a random-intercept mixed model gives valid intervals because its model-based variance does not rest on unit-level residuals.
regime: inference; continuous outcome; G < 8 clusters
decision: exit offered from the refused table

claimed_basis: WP12 (turbotab/core/models/repeated.py); test_wp2 reference (MixedLM p = 0.85 vs independent OLS p ~ 4e-14)

Other exits: combine each unit's rows; shared-frailty Cox / random-intercept logistic (not built; 'one survival time per unit: combining rows is no answer', inference.py:259). Related: the causal lane says a random-intercept mixed model does not repair its own below-floor case (stages/causal.py:396, S7-037).

statement: For least squares with rows clustered by unit, CR2 (bias-reduced linearization) standard errors with t reference distributions on Bell-McCaffrey Satterthwaite degrees of freedom (working model of independent, equal-variance rows) give close to nominal type-I error and coverage even with few clusters (G >= 8).

Not tested at G = 8-11 or with strongly unbalanced clusters. Docstring inference.py:11-17. Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (Corrected) 'Repeated units or clusters imply ... a small-sample sandwich (CR2, Bell–McCaffrey df) with refusal below a floor' (the floor is S3-056).

notes: Known-truth simulation (randomized binary exposure, n = 200,000) covers the logistic OR only; HR, cumulative OR and multinomial RRR are not simulated (test_estimand_chain.py::test_b_a_cause_of_the_outcome_only_changes_the_conditional_hazard_ratio_and_the_app_says_so checks wording only). The note does not block the adjustment; it is shown on the one-tap block before confirmation. Other locations: turbotab/core/estimand.py:329 (NON_COLLAPSIBLE), 409-411, 1299-1305 (caption 'a conditional ratio, which changes with the covariates even without confounding'); turbotab/core/models/effects.py:7-10; turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1797. Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (New) 'adding a precision covariate under an OR or HR changes the conditional estimand, and the app says so'.

statement: For a yes/no outcome, the marginal risk difference and risk ratio of the declared exposure contrast are estimated by fitting the maximum-likelihood logistic model on the pipeline's model matrix and averaging every analyzed row's predicted risk with the exposure set to each setting: RD = mean_i expit(x_i(1)'b) - mean_i expit(x_i(0)'b) and RR = their ratio.
regime: inference; binary outcome; logistic family on the model matrix (standardizes_risks); no survey design, no multiple imputation
decision: the marginal measures reported by the effects stage
user_sees: The marginal risk difference and risk ratio (...) were estimated by standardization over the analyzed rows (g-computation) from the logistic model
claimed_basis: Daniel, Zhang & Farewell 2021; MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 9
notes: R glm + mean(predict(type='response')) reference by definition (also numpy by hand). Standardization population is all analyzed rows. The estimand.py module docstring (turbotab/core/estimand.py:31-33) still says the marginal RD/RR are 'named and refused, never answered with an odds ratio', stale relative to the code that fits them. Other tasks: refused ('a marginal risk difference is standardized here from a yes/no outcome's logistic model only', turbotab/core/estimand.py:340-345). Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:7-23, 335-341; turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1037-1139.

statement: For a continuous exposure, the marginal contrast matching its per-unit odds ratio is every analyzed row's observed exposure raised by one unit against the observed exposure; a two-valued numeric exposure is set to its higher against its lower value, and a categorical exposure each level against the first.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal RD/RR declared
user_sees: setting label 'one unit higher than observed' | '`1` against `0`' | '`b` against `a`'
claimed_basis: none stated beyond the docstring ('the per-unit scale of its odds ratio')
notes: The R test confirms the shift is computed, not that it is the right estimand. An incremental (+1) shift on a nonlinear model gives a population-average effect that depends on the exposure distribution; under a spline the same one-unit standardization is used for sensitivity (turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1360-1368).

statement: A 95% percentile interval from 1,000 nonparametric bootstrap resamples, each refitting the whole pipeline (energy model, forms, missing-value fill) and the logistic model, with whole units resampled when rows repeat, is a valid interval for the marginal risk difference and risk ratio.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal measure declared; units at or above the unit floor
user_sees: with 95% percentile intervals from 1,000 bootstrap resamples refitting the whole chain by `pid`
claimed_basis: Efron & Tibshirani 1993 §13.3 (B = 1,000 for a percentile interval); contract relation gcomp-bootstrap-chain (turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1841-1845)
notes: test_estimand_2_g_computation.py::test_2_the_interval_is_the_whole_chain_bootstrap_percentile and ::test_2_rows_that_repeat_are_resampled_by_whole_unit recompute the same procedure on the same resamples (pin the code to its convention), not coverage. Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:432-442, 470-526; turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1048-1051, 1095-1101.

statement: A bootstrap resample whose outcome is separated by the covariates should be kept at the logistic likelihood's supremum (separated rows' risks 0 or 1, the rest fit by maximum likelihood), the fit R's glm approaches, rather than dropped, because dropping such resamples removes the interval's most extreme draws.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal measure declared; bootstrap resamples with quasi or complete separation (sparse levels)
decision: how separated resamples enter the marginal intervals
user_sees: Each is kept at the likelihood's limit, where the separated rows' risks are 0 or 1, the fit R's glm approaches as its coefficients run away; leaving them out would cut the interval's most extreme resa
claimed_basis: Konis 2007 (separation detection by linear programs); none stated for the interval claim
notes: test_estimand_2_g_computation.py::test_2_separated_resamples_agree_with_r_glm_on_the_same_resamples and ::test_2_a_separated_resample_is_kept_at_the_likelihoods_limit_numpy_by_hand check that the limit equals R glm run to its limit / the saturated model's shares, not that keeping them gives the right coverage. A RR with zero low risk becomes +inf and the upper limit unbounded. Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:198-238, 300-332; turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1147-1154.

statement: When rows repeat within fewer units than the unit floor, a cluster bootstrap of the marginal risks is no more reliable (too narrow) than the cluster-robust sandwich the fit refuses, so the marginal risks are reported without any interval.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal measure; clustered or repeated rows with units below inference.min_clusters
decision: whether the marginal risks carry an interval
user_sees: no interval is reported (`site` has 4 units, fewer than the ... TurboTab requires for cluster-robust intervals ...)
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (repeated units imply a small-sample sandwich 'with refusal below a floor'); code comment 'a bootstrap of a handful of units is as narrow as the sandwich the fit refuses'
notes: test_estimand_2_g_computation.py::test_2_below_the_unit_floor_the_marginal_risks_carry_no_interval checks the refusal appears, not the reason. The floor value lives in models/inference.py (other slice).

statement: Under a surveyed-population estimand, g-computation standardized over the sampled participants without the design does not estimate the population's marginal risks, so the marginal risk difference or ratio is blocked and recorded (exits: the sample-only answer or the design-based conditional odds ratio).
regime: inference; binary outcome; survey design with the population answer
user_sees: The marginal risks are standardized over these participants; no design-based standardization over the surveyed population is built here.
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 6; §4 'Population estimand without a design-based estimator: block and record'
notes: test_estimand_2_g_computation.py::test_2_a_surveyed_population_blocks_the_marginal_risks_and_records_the_way_out checks the block only. Weighted standardization exists in the literature; the claim is that it is required, not that it is impossible. Also turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1053-1057, 1850-1853.

statement: Under multiple imputation, a valid interval for the g-computation marginal risks would require repeating the imputation within every bootstrap resample, so the marginal risks are not reported under multiple imputation and the conditional odds ratio is offered instead.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal measure; missing values handled by multiple imputation
user_sees: The marginal risks are not pooled over multiple imputations here: the bootstrap would have to repeat the imputation in every resample.
claimed_basis: none stated
notes: Referee: whether bootstrap-within-each-imputation then pooling (or Rubin's rules on per-copy bootstrap variances) is an acceptable alternative (e.g. Schomaker & Heumann 2018); the 'would have to' framing may be overstated.

statement: Under the all-components energy model, a substitution moves several energy sources at once (a weighted contrast of coefficients), so marginal standardization of a one-unit change in the exposure column does not estimate the substitution; the conditional model's average relative effect carries it instead.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal measure; energy-bearing exposure; substitution contrast; all-components energy model
user_sees: Under the all-components model a substitution moves several energy sources at once (a weighted contrast); its standardization is not built here. The conditional odds ratio's average relative effect ca
claimed_basis: implied Tomova et al. 2022 (BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 2)
notes: Overlaps the energy slice (methods/energy.py relative_effect_rows).

statement: Under the partition energy model with an addition contrast, the counterfactual 'one unit more of the exposure' must also raise total energy by the exposure's kcal per unit, so that energy from the other sources stays fixed, because the partition model derives other-source energy from the total.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal measure; energy-bearing exposure; addition contrast; partition model
decision: how the high setting is built for g-computation
user_sees: (no sentence; changes the marginal RD/RR numbers under addition)
claimed_basis: none stated (docstring of counterfactual)
notes: Also turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1079-1084. Overlaps the energy slice.

statement: In a model built to estimate the exposure's effect only the exposure's coefficients are effect estimates; every other coefficient is at best a direct effect and may be confounded even where the exposure's estimate is not, so all other rows are listed apart as 'adjustment terms, not effect estimates' (the Table 2 fallacy).
regime: inference; every family with a coefficient table; declared estimand
decision: what the results table shows as effects
user_sees: adjustment terms, not effect estimates | an adjustment term: a direct effect at best, and possibly confounded even where the estimate of what you study is not
claimed_basis: Westreich & Greenland 2013, Am J Epidemiol 177:292; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11
notes: test_estimand_3_table2.py::test_3_every_other_row_is_an_adjustment_term_in_the_appendix checks the display only. Also: a declared modifier's main effect is never an effect ('the effect of what you study is read within its levels'), the intercept is 'the model's baseline'. Other locations: turbotab/core/estimand.py:1619-1664 (annotate_fit), turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:789-806, 1683-1684.

statement: The sound and customary inference presentation is a declared sequence shown for the exposure only: the unadjusted estimate always (STROBE 16a), Model 1 holding the field's age, sex and energy, Model 2 = the primary full adjustment set derived from the answers, and an optional Model 3 adding the possible mediators or unknown-timing covariates, labeled as not a total effect.
regime: inference; declared exposure and adjustment answers; families with a model-matrix table
decision: the declared model sequence (Table 2) and the Model 1 guess
user_sees: The field's Model 1 adjusts for age, sex and energy (NUTRITION_PACK §08); say which columns those are. Model 2 is the primary, Model 3 adds the possible mediators your answers set beside it.
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11; STROBE item 16a; NUTRITION_PACK §08; contract label 'customary: the nutrition-cohort Table 2 (Westreich & Greenland 2013)'
notes: Model 1 guess reads names age/sex/gender/RIDAGEYR/RIAGENDR plus the energy role (a proposal, one tap); Model 1 must be a subset of the primary's adjusted set ('so each model adds to the one before'), else refused (turbotab/core/estimand.py:2344-2355). Also turbotab/core/estimand.py:1335-1397, turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:733-735, 988-1004, 1860-1872.

statement: Refitting the unadjusted model and Model 1 as column subsets of the primary pipeline's own model matrix (energy model, forms, knots and missing-value fill fitted once on all rows with the full covariate set) gives valid unadjusted and partially adjusted estimates, because the exposure's definition stays identical across models.
regime: inference; declared sequence; any energy model, form or fill
decision: how the crude model and Model 1 are fit
user_sees: The estimate of `fiber` is reported across a declared sequence of models fit on all N analyzed rows: unadjusted; Model 1, adjusted for `age` and `sex`; Model 2, the primary, ...
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11; contract scope note 'the exposure's definition fitted once' (turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1862)
notes: test_estimand_3_table2.py::test_3_each_declared_model_shows_the_exposure_only_and_agrees_with_statsmodels compares with OLS on raw designs for a plain exposure only. Where the exposure is an energy-adjusted residual, a density, or imputed using the covariates and outcome, the 'unadjusted' model still carries covariate information through the transform or fill; referee should check whether it is then 'unadjusted'. Also turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:722-753.

statement: When a further-adjusted model's added columns (Model 3, or the secondary 'further adjusted for' model) are missing on some rows under complete cases, the comparison model must be refit on the same reduced rows so the two estimates differ by the added adjustment alone, not by the change of sample.
regime: inference; complete-case analysis; secondary/Model 3 columns sometimes missing
decision: the rows the secondary comparison is fit on
user_sees: The primary's adjustment refit on Model 3's {m} rows, so Model 3 differs from it by `bmi` alone.
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 3 (every analyzed row); contract relation model3-own-rows (turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1891-1895)
notes: test_estimand_3_table2.py::test_3_model_2_is_the_fits_primary_and_model_3_alone_takes_fewer_rows confirms the computation. The effects stage keeps Model 2 on all rows and adds the same-rows comparison; the secondary stage (turbotab/core/stages/secondary.py:112-117) refits the primary itself on the reduced rows, so the two surfaces differ. Under MI each further-adjusted model is imputed with its added columns in the imputation model (turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:43-44, 569-582; turbotab/core/stages/secondary.py:14-15).

statement: Under multiple imputation, the proportional-hazards and influence diagnostics and the Cinelli-Hazlett robustness value can be read from the first completed copy alone (labeled so) rather than combined across copies.
regime: inference; multiple imputation
decision: the diagnostics and robustness value under MI
user_sees: (on the first of the completed copies) | The robustness value reads the first completed copy.
claimed_basis: none stated
notes: Also turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:44-45, 1527-1528. A single copy understates missing-data uncertainty; referee: is one copy representative for a pass/fail diagnostic.

statement: When the data arrive as stacked imputed copies (an implicate column), fitting the declared models, marginal risks, diagnostics or sensitivity analyses on the stacked rows would count each participant once per copy and leave out the between-copy variance, so these are withheld and only the Rubin's-rules pooled primary is reported.
regime: inference; data with supplied imputed copies kept as rows
decision: whether the effects stage's analyses are built
user_sees: fit on the copies stacked, each participant would count once per copy and every interval would leave out the variation between the copies.
claimed_basis: contract relation sequence-supplied-copies (turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1900-1904)
notes: Also turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:489-494. Merged duplicate: the causal lane refuses stacked imputed copies for the same reason (stages/causal.py:416). Related: S8-045 (combining copies per unit), S3-046 (per-copy analysis pooled by Rubin's rules).

statement: Under the surveyed-population answer every declared model (unadjusted, Model 1-3) must be design-based (weighted, Taylor-linearized over strata and PSUs) for its estimates to describe the surveyed population; a family without a design-based estimator is blocked and recorded, never shown as an unweighted refit beside a design-based primary.
regime: inference; survey design with the population answer
user_sees: Each model is design-based: weighted by `wt`, with Taylor-linearized intervals over the survey's strata and PSUs, so the estimates describe the surveyed population.
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 6 ('binds every family and every display'); contract relation sequence-design-based
notes: test_estimand_3_table2.py::test_3_under_the_surveyed_population_every_model_is_design_based checks each model against R survey (computation), which would not fail if the ruling were wrong. Also turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1686-1690, 1896-1899.

statement: The proportional-hazards check is the Grambsch-Therneau score test of gamma = 0 for each term's covariates times g(t) = 1 - KM(t-) centered over the events, with Efron ties and counting-process risk sets under delayed entry, per term and global, as R's survival::cox.zph (version 3.0 or later, default 'km' transform) computes it.
regime: inference; time-to-event outcome; Cox family
user_sees: Proportional hazards by Schoenfeld residuals: the score test of each term's product with a function of time (one minus the Kaplan-Meier estimate), as R's cox.zph computes it
claimed_basis: Grambsch & Therneau 1994, Biometrika 81:515; R survival::cox.zph
notes: R reference to 1e-6, with and without ties and delayed entry. Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:561-586 (time_scale); turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1203-1224.

statement: A proportional-hazards failure of the exposure is declared when the cox.zph score test of the exposure's own term (not the global test or the covariates' terms) has p < 0.05, the customary level; the failure then carries response exits.
regime: inference; time-to-event outcome; Cox family
decision: whether the PH check is 'failed' and response exits are offered
user_sees: The hazard ratio of what you study changes over follow-up (chi2(1) = ..., p = ..., below the customary 0.05): the reported ratio is an average over follow-up.
claimed_basis: PH_ALPHA = 0.05 'at the customary level' (turbotab/core/models/effects.py:88); MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11
notes: test_estimand_4_diagnostics.py::test_4_proportional_hazards_agree_with_cox_zph asserts one simulated non-PH exposure is detected (power on one case), not the rule. A significance test at large n flags trivial departures and at small n misses large ones; covariates' PH failures do not fail the check. Inconsistent thresholds: the fit stage's proportional-hazards warning uses p < 0.01/P (models/survival.py:518, S7-042), this stage p < 0.05 on the exposure's term.

statement: When the exposure's proportional-hazards check fails, the recommended response is to report its hazard ratio before and after the median event time (follow-up split there by episode, the exposure's product with the later period added) beside the overall estimate, because the ratio is then shown where it holds.
regime: inference; time-to-event; failed PH check of a single-column exposure
decision: the recorded response to a failed PH check
user_sees: The hazard ratio before and after {cut}, the median event time: follow-up split there, the product of what you study with the later period added.
claimed_basis: contract: 'customary for a proportional-hazards failure (Grambsch & Therneau 1994)', 'Sound: the ratio is shown where it holds', rung recommended (turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1921-1923)
notes: test_estimand_4_diagnostics.py::test_4_a_failed_check_records_hazard_ratios_before_and_after_the_cut matches R survSplit + coxph (computation only). The median event time cut is a convention; 'where it holds' assumes a constant HR within each period. Keep-labeled is the other exit. Also turbotab/core/estimand.py:1402-1415.

statement: In the episode-split Cox model, one person's split rows never overlap in time, so the partial likelihood is the time-varying-covariate one and the model-based Wald intervals of the period hazard ratios are valid without clustering by person.
regime: inference; time-to-event; period hazard ratios after a failed PH check
decision: the intervals of the period hazard ratios
user_sees: (intervals of the before/after hazard ratios)
claimed_basis: none stated (docstring)
notes: The R reference uses coxph without cluster(id), so agreement checks computation only.

statement: A row is influential when its Cook's distance exceeds the median of F(p, n - p) (p the model's rank), Cook's (1977) reference for a deletion that moves the estimates to the edge of their 50% confidence region; the same reference is applied to a logistic model's Cook's distance from Pearson residuals.
regime: inference; least-squares or logistic primary model
decision: whether the influence check fails and exits are offered
user_sees: {k} rows move the estimates past Cook's reference (largest distance ..., against ...).
claimed_basis: Cook 1977, Technometrics 19:15; R's plot.lm contours
notes: Leverage and D themselves agree with R hatvalues/cooks.distance (test_estimand_4_diagnostics.py::test_4_leverage_and_cooks_distance_agree_with_r, which also checks one planted OLS row is the only one flagged). The 50% region reading is exact for OLS only; for logistic it is an approximation. Any flagged row fails the check, whether or not it moves the exposure's coefficient, yet the methods text says 'the check failed for the exposure'. Also turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1260-1307.

statement: For a failed influence check, refitting the primary model without all the flagged rows is sound only as a sensitivity analysis shown beside the primary, never in its place; keeping the estimate labeled with the failed check is also sound.
regime: inference; failed influence check
decision: the recorded response to a failed influence check
user_sees: The primary model refit without the {k} influential rows, on {n} rows.
claimed_basis: contract: 'customary for influential rows (Cook 1977)', 'Sound as a sensitivity analysis beside the primary, never in its place' (turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1918-1927)
notes: test_estimand_4_diagnostics.py::test_4_an_influential_row_fails_the_check_and_its_response_refits_without_it checks the refit computation. Also turbotab/core/estimand.py:1402-1411.

statement: The E-value of a risk ratio RR >= 1 is RR + sqrt(RR(RR - 1)) (of 1/RR when RR < 1), reported for the estimate and for the confidence limit nearer the null (1 when the interval includes the null).
regime: inference; any ratio estimate converted to the risk-ratio scale
decision: the E-value shown for every inference estimate
user_sees: E-value for the estimate: 2.31, and for the confidence limit nearer the null 1.62 (VanderWeele & Ding 2017, Ann Intern Med 167:268)
claimed_basis: VanderWeele & Ding 2017; R EValue package
notes: R EValue reference to 1e-8 including a null-crossing interval. Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:807-839, turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1569-1580.

statement: An odds ratio or hazard ratio approximates a risk ratio when the outcome is rare (event share below 15%) and is used as is; for a common outcome the odds ratio is converted by sqrt(OR) and the hazard ratio by (1 - 0.5^sqrt(HR))/(1 - 0.5^sqrt(1/HR)) before the E-value is computed.
regime: inference; binary or time-to-event outcome; conditional OR or HR reported; rare/common decided by the event's share among analyzed rows (design-weighted under the population answer)
user_sees: E-value for the estimate: ..., and for the confidence limit nearer the null ...; an E-value is read against the common causes one can name, never as a pass or a fail.
claimed_basis: VanderWeele & Ding 2017 ('<15% at the end of follow-up'); R EValue conversions; RARE_OUTCOME = 0.15 at turbotab/core/models/effects.py:84
notes: The test checks the conversions given a rare flag (they equal EValue's), not the 15% rule or how the share is computed. For a time-to-event outcome the share is the crude fraction of analyzed rows with an event, ignoring censoring and follow-up length, which may misclassify a common outcome as rare. Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:1105, turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1411-1421, 1499-1504.

statement: A linear coefficient b is put on the risk-ratio scale for its E-value as the standardized difference d = b*delta/SD (delta = 1 unit), RR ~ exp(0.91 d), with interval exp(0.91 d +/- 1.78 se_d).
regime: inference; numeric outcome; least-squares or other mean-difference families
user_sees: E-value for the estimate: ...
claimed_basis: VanderWeele & Ding 2017's approximation; R EValue::evalues.OLS
notes: Test checks the formula equals evalues.OLS; the 0.91 approximation's validity (it assumes an approximately normal outcome and a binary dichotomization argument) is not tested. Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:800-803.

statement: The SD that standardizes a difference for its E-value is the SD of the outcome the estimand speaks of: the analyzed rows' marginal outcome SD (ddof = 1) under the sample answer, and the design-weighted population SD (R survey svyvar: n/(n-1) * sum w(y - ybar_w)^2 / sum w over positive-weight rows) under the surveyed-population answer, the same in the effects stage and the causal lane.
regime: inference; numeric outcome; sample or surveyed-population answer
decision: which SD the E-value of a difference uses
user_sees: Sensitivity ... by the E-value ..., the difference standardized by the outcome's design-weighted standard deviation in the surveyed population
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 14; VanderWeele & Ding 2017
notes: test_causal_lane.py::test_7_a_survey_design_and_multiple_imputation_in_the_chain checks the svyvar formula against R (computation), not the choice of the marginal outcome SD over the residual SD (EValue documentation allows either, with different meanings). Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:842-848; turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1423-1437, 1457-1462, 1590-1594. Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 14 (VanderWeele & Ding 2017's RR ≈ exp(0.91·d); 'The effects stage and the causal lane use the same SD'). Merged duplicate: the causal lane applies the same SD rule (stages/causal.py:813).

statement: For a least-squares outcome under inference, the Cinelli-Hazlett robustness value benchmarked against each named, measured, adjusted covariate should rank before the E-value, because it is anchored to the study's own covariates; a sensitivity analysis is offered for every reported inference estimate.
regime: inference; numeric outcome; least-squares family on the model matrix
user_sees: An unmeasured common cause would need a partial R2 of 4.1% with both `fiber` and `glucose`, beyond the measured covariates, to bring the estimate to zero (Cinelli & Hazlett 2020...)
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 10; Cinelli & Hazlett 2020, J R Stat Soc B 82:39; contract option 'Sound: bounded by named measured covariates; ranked first for a linear outcome'
notes: test_estimand_5_sensitivity.py::test_5_the_stage_offers_it_for_a_linear_outcome_robustness_value_first and ::test_5_the_function_the_causal_lane_calls_ranks_the_robustness_value_first check the order only. Benchmarking against measured covariates assumes the unmeasured confounder is comparable to them (Cinelli & Hazlett caution). Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:1107-1116, turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1956-1968. Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 10 (offered for every inference result, required in the causal lane; E-value never with a pass/fail threshold, see S6-035).

statement: The robustness value RV_q = 2/(1 + sqrt(1 + 4/f_q^2)) with f_q = q|t|/sqrt(dof), RV_{q,alpha}, the exposure's partial R2 t^2/(t^2 + dof), and the bounds and bias-adjusted estimate for a confounder kd times as strong as a measured benchmark covariate (r2dz = kd*r2dxj/(1 - r2dxj), ...) are Cinelli & Hazlett's (2020) quantities as sensemakr computes them, with each adjusted covariate (a categorical one as its indicator group) as a benchmark at kd = 1.
regime: inference; numeric outcome; one unweighted least-squares coefficient
decision: the robustness value and benchmark rows
user_sees: ; one as strong as `smoking` would move it to 0.21 (95% CI ...)
claimed_basis: Cinelli & Hazlett 2020; R sensemakr 0.1.6
notes: R sensemakr reference to 1e-8 with a single-column and a three-level benchmark. The reading quotes the benchmark that moves the estimate most (turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1560-1565). Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:851-914, 976-1043, turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1507-1520.

statement: RV_{q,alpha} and the benchmarks' adjusted intervals rest on the classical least-squares standard error, so when the interval shown is HC3, cluster-robust or MI-pooled they must not be reported, while the partial R2, RV_q, the bounds and the adjusted point estimates stay valid whatever standard error is shown.
regime: inference; numeric outcome; least-squares; non-classical reported covariance (the default HC3)
user_sees: The robustness value for the 95% interval and the benchmarks' adjusted intervals rest on the classical least-squares standard error (...), as sensemakr computes them; the interval reported uses HC3
claimed_basis: Cinelli & Hazlett 2020 §4 (omitted-variable bias algebra of the point estimate); contract relation rv-interval-classical
notes: test_estimand_5_sensitivity.py::test_5_the_stage_offers_it_for_a_linear_outcome_robustness_value_first checks the note and rv_alpha None. Since the linear family's default interval is HC3, RV_{q,alpha} is usually withheld. Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:933-948, turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1613-1627, 1971-1974. Merged duplicate: the causal lane's partially linear model applies the same restriction (causal.py:549).

statement: The robustness value is defined only for one unweighted least-squares coefficient, so it is not computed for a family that does not fit by least squares, for a survey-weighted fit, or for the all-components model's average relative effect (a contrast of several coefficients).
regime: inference; numeric outcome
decision: whether a robustness value is reported
user_sees: No robustness value: the robustness value is defined for an unweighted least-squares fit.
claimed_basis: Cinelli & Hazlett 2020
notes: Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:56-61. The E-value is still given in these cases.

statement: No E-value or robustness value is defined for a conditional cumulative odds ratio (ordinal outcome) or a multinomial relative-risk ratio (multiclass outcome), so no unmeasured-confounding sensitivity is reported for them.
regime: inference; ordinal or multiclass outcome
decision: whether a sensitivity analysis is reported
user_sees: No E-value or robustness value is defined here for a conditional cumulative odds ratio.
claimed_basis: none stated
notes: Conflicts with ruling 10's 'offered for every inference result'. The E-value applies to any risk/odds-type ratio with the rare/common conversion (VanderWeele & Ding 2017), so a cumulative OR or a category-vs-reference RRR could be bounded.

statement: When the marginal risk difference or ratio is declared, the unmeasured-confounding E-value is computed on the marginal risk ratio with its bootstrap limits rather than on the conditional odds ratio, since a risk difference has no E-value without its risks.
regime: inference; binary outcome; marginal measure declared
user_sees: E-value for the marginal risk ratio: ..., and for the confidence limit nearer the null ...
claimed_basis: VanderWeele & Ding 2017
notes: test_estimand_2_g_computation.py::test_2_below_the_unit_floor... checks the computed value only. Also turbotab/core/models/effects.py:1096-1097, turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1496-1498.

statement: When the exposure enters as a restricted cubic spline, which no single coefficient carries, the unmeasured-confounding sensitivity can be run on the straight-line estimate from the same model with the spline's nonlinear terms left out (or, under a declared marginal measure, on the curve's one-unit standardization) and stated as such.
regime: inference; spline exposure
decision: what the sensitivity analysis bounds for a curve
user_sees: What you study enters as a curve (a restricted cubic spline), which no single coefficient carries; this analysis bounds the straight-line estimate beside it, the same model with the spline's nonlinear
claimed_basis: contract relation curve-straight-line (turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:1975-1977); none external
notes: test_estimand_5_sensitivity.py::test_5_a_curve_is_bounded_through_its_straight_line_estimate checks computation. The straight line is a different estimand from the curve; its bound may not bound the curve's contrasts. Also turbotab/core/stages/effects.py:736-740.

statement: For an exposure family under inference, Benjamini-Hochberg q-values (controlling the expected share of false discoveries among the tests, every member shown) are the sound default multiplicity method.
regime: inference; two or more exposures reported each in turn (feature-wise family)
decision: the family's multiplicity method when none is named
user_sees: Benjamini-Hochberg q-values control the false-discovery rate across all {n} (Benjamini & Hochberg 1995, J R Stat Soc B 57:289), and every member is shown, significant or not.
claimed_basis: Benjamini & Hochberg 1995; MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 ('An exposure family implies multiplicity control: BH q-values for feature-wise analyses'); METABOLOMICS_PACK §08
notes: BH controls FDR under independence or positive dependence (PRDS); correlated nutrients may violate it. Overlaps methods/omics.py (other slice). Also turbotab/core/estimand.py:1085-1124. Doc: MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (New) 'An exposure family implies multiplicity control: BH q-values for feature-wise analyses; for a few prespecified nutrient hypotheses, the number of tests stated'. Under MI the q-values are computed on Rubin-pooled p-values (S3-034).

statement: Unadjusted p-values with the number of tests stated are customary and conditionally sound only for a few (at most 10) declared nutrient hypotheses (Rothman 1990); for an omics family at any size, or beyond 10 tests, they are blocked and recorded because n tests at p < 0.05 give about 0.05*n false positives by chance alone.
regime: inference; exposure family; multiplicity 'count_stated'
decision: whether unadjusted family p-values are accepted
user_sees: A family of 40 study factors reported by unadjusted p-values gives about 2 false positives at p < 0.05 by chance alone; the number of tests stated is customary for a few declared hypotheses (Rothman 1
claimed_basis: Rothman 1990, Epidemiology 1:43; METABOLOMICS_PACK §08 ('a fatal flaw in review'); MULTIPLICITY_SMALL = 10, 'the app's convention' (methods/omics.py:1653)
notes: 'About 0.05*n false positives' is the expected count only when every null is true. test_estimand_6_families.py::test_6_bh_is_declared_unless_another_method_is_and_an_omics_family_without_it_is_recorded checks the refusal. Also turbotab/core/estimand.py:1085-1124, methods/omics.py:1680-1690.

statement: An exposure family's estimand (each exposure in turn, adjusted for the covariates but not for the other exposures) is estimated only by fitting each exposure separately; a joint model that adjusts each exposure for the others estimates a different estimand.
regime: inference; exposure family declared
decision: which model families may be selected
user_sees: The comparison you want is each study factor in turn, adjusted for the covariates; `linear` adjusts each study factor for the others, which is a different comparison.
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 2
notes: Also turbotab/core/estimand.py:1195-1201.

statement: For a yes/no outcome beside a numeric column that reads as follow-up time and varies (range above 5% of its maximum), analyzing the outcome as yes/no counts people who left or whose study ended before their event as having none, so 'everyone was followed equally long' is blocked until attested and a time-to-event model is offered instead.
regime: binary outcome; a follow-up-like numeric column whose values vary; inference or prediction
decision: the follow-up answer (yes/no vs time to event)
user_sees: `followup_years` reads as a follow-up time and runs from 0.3 to 14.9: if it is how long each person was followed, some left or the study ended before their event could be seen, and a yes/no model
claimed_basis: PROBAST explanation and elaboration (Moons et al. 2019), item 4.6
notes: The 'varies' rule ((max - min) > 0.05*max) is a convention (turbotab/core/estimand.py:142-160). PROBAST 4.6 speaks of prognostic models; the app applies it under inference too. Refusal tests (test_wp17_purpose_routes.py) check the block only.

statement: Under the clinical or dietary lens (or no lens), a yes/no outcome is often an event followed over time and is always asked about its follow-up, while under an assay or survey lens alone a yes/no outcome is a status at sampling and is read as counted over one period for everyone unless some column reads as follow-up time.
regime: binary outcome; lens declared
decision: whether the follow-up question is asked or skipped
user_sees: no numeric column reads as a follow-up time, and under this lens a yes/no outcome is a status at sampling, so it is read as counted over one period for everyone.
claimed_basis: routing gate finding (NHANES linked mortality MORTSTAT/PERMTH_INT fit as logistic)
notes: Also turbotab/core/estimand.py:183-212.

statement: A column named as a time-to-event outcome's follow-up time is part of the outcome itself and cannot also be a predictor of it.
regime: time-to-event outcome with a declared follow-up column
user_sees: `PERMTH_INT` is named as `MORTSTAT`'s follow-up (the follow-up question), part of the outcome itself, so it cannot also predict it.
claimed_basis: routing gate (PERMTH_INT proposed as an exposure)

statement: Under inference, declaring that nothing groups the participants when a column reads as a site, centre, household or batch is blocked and recorded, because people within one group are more alike than across groups, so intervals that treat rows as independent are too narrow, and between-group differences can confound the exposure.
regime: inference; a named or structurally guessed grouping column
user_sees: People in one site or household are more alike than people across them, so intervals that treat them as independent are too narrow, and between-group differences can confound what you study.
claimed_basis: audit RO-08 ('adjust and cluster, or record why not')
notes: A column guessed from its values alone may be confirmed 'marks no group' without a limitation. test_wp17_purpose_routes.py::test_4_a_cluster_question_fires_and_site_fixed_effects_reproduce_the_audit checks the refusal code only for this part.

statement: Under inference, the recommended handling of a grouping of participants is an intercept per group (fixed effects) plus intervals clustered by it (CR2 with Bell-McCaffrey df); clustering the intervals alone is a lesser option offered with its concern.
regime: inference; a column the user says groups the participants
decision: how a grouping enters the model
user_sees: Under inference participants in one `site` share more than chance: say whether each `site` gets its own intercept as well as clustered intervals.
claimed_basis: audit RO-08; MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (repeated units imply cluster-aware intervals, CR2 with Bell-McCaffrey df)
notes: test_wp17_purpose_routes.py::test_4_a_cluster_question_fires_and_site_fixed_effects_reproduce_the_audit checks CR2 by definition and that it is wider than z with <= 12 clusters (computation), not that FE+cluster beats cluster-only. Fixed effects change the estimand to within-group and drop group-level exposures. CR2 claims belong to models/inference.py (other slice). Also turbotab/core/estimand.py:22-25, 258-269.

statement: Under prediction a grouping of participants decides how the rows are validated (whole groups kept together, internal-external validation across groups), not the model's intercepts, so fixed-effects or cluster-only adjustment is refused.
regime: prediction; a grouping column
user_sees: Under prediction a grouping decides how the rows are validated (by whole groups, and across groups), not the model's intercepts; it is recorded without them.
claimed_basis: audit RO-08; MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (prediction: grouped folds and holdout, performance heterogeneity across sites)

statement: Under inference no coefficient, curve, contrast, refit, explanation or diagnostic response may be shown until the follow-up, the grouping, the exposure and its effect, every covariate's adjustment answers, the forms and any time-varying lane are declared, because the reported model must not be chosen from the data it reports on.
regime: inference; any open plan question
decision: what the server serves while the plan is open
user_sees: No estimate is shown until the adjustment set is answered: each covariate's answers decide whether it is adjusted for, left out or set beside the primary.
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE organizing fact ('Inference may not choose its model from the data it will report on') and §4 ('required: no estimates until answered'); §1 row 12 (the analysis-plan lock)
notes: Also: a diagnostic response is refused before the plan is locked ('saying whether one failed would be the first sight of the fit', turbotab/core/estimand.py:2382-2388); the time-varying lane's weight truncation is declared 'after the diagnostics are read, before any estimate'.
